Chapter 1: Introduction and overview

Navigating this guidance product

1.1 This guidance has been structured to help you find information or the action you need to take, as quickly as possible. All chapters of this product are contained in a single document, so you can use search options such as:

web-links provided on the left side of this page

control F (Ctrl-F) to search for key words

the ‘Find’ option (see 3 dots) at the top right of the page

in addition, when searching for key words, the glossary will help in terms of summarising or providing a key search-word or phrase

1.2 The Confident Futures provider guidance will sometimes use the term “you” or “your” to mean the providers of the Confident Futures Support. Likewise, it will sometimes say “we” to mean Department of Work and Pensions (DWP).

1.3 The guidance is set out in sections based on the Participants’ journey throughout their time on Confident Futures following:

joining Confident Futures

during Confident Futures

leaving Confident Futures

1.4 Guidance relevant to aspects of Confident Futures that can cover any stage of Confident Futures, such as IT and Performance Management, are grouped together in a separate section.

Note: The Generic provider guidance on GOV.UK is not linked and should not be referenced in relation to Confident Futures.

Introduction to DWP

1.5 DWP is responsible for welfare, pensions and child maintenance policy. As the UK’s biggest public service department, it administers the State Pension and a range of working age, disability and ill health benefits to around 20 million Claimants and customers. Read further information about DWP.

Aims of DWP provision

1.6 DWP’s Contracted Employment Provision aims to deliver the best possible service to the people who are Participants on DWP programmes. Read the values and aims of DWP.

1.7 The aim of DWP Contracted Employment Provision is to support these values by helping and supporting people who are out of work to move into and remain in employment, recognising work as the primary sustainable route out of poverty and reducing the number of children in workless households.

1.8 Your performance contributes directly to that of DWP overall and we therefore have a shared interest in the success of your provision. DWP operates a policy of continuous improvement in which we work to raise all aspects of quality and performance in the services we deliver, and you are expected to work with us in doing so.

1.9 All DWP provision is designed to tackle specific barriers that unemployed people face in finding and retaining work. You are expected to provide people with a professional, high quality, personalised and work-like experience that delivers a sense of pace and purpose in their efforts to find work.

The DWP Customer Charter

1.10 DWP is committed to providing high quality and efficient services to our customers. The DWP Customer Charter sets out the standards that customers can expect and what their responsibilities are in return.

1.11 DWP is dedicated to raising the standards of all our contracted provision and require all providers and sub-contractors to embed the principles of the Customer Charter into the services you deliver on DWP’s behalf. The ‘shared promise on customer care’, developed by the Employment Related Services Association and supported by DWP, makes the commitments given in the DWP Customer Charter more specific for welfare to work providers to enable them to sign the Shared Promise. DWP will expect you and your sub-contractors to support the commitments contained in it.

1.12 In addition to the above, an outline of what your responsibilities are in return, can be found in DWP procurement policies and procedures.

The Disability Confident Scheme

1.13 Providers will clearly demonstrate that they are playing a significant role in developing the confidence of employers to accommodate disabled people in their workplace and understand the principles of Disability Confident.

1.14 Disability Confident is creating a movement of change, encouraging employers to think differently about disability and take action to improve how they recruit, retain and develop disabled employees.

1.15 As Disability Confident Leaders, providers will be showing disabled people that they are serious about leading the way and helping other businesses become Disability Confident. More information can be found on Disability Confident – how to sign up the employer scheme.

1.16 This provider guidance is not a contractual document however it is intended to help you to deliver the service as outlined in your contract.

1.17 It uses different terms depending where someone is in relation to their journey on the provision:

whilst a person is being considered for referral, they will be referred to as a “Claimant” by Jobcentre Plus until the point at which they attend their Initial Meeting and start on the provision

after attending their Initial Meeting, either face to face or through the Claimant’s preferred mode of contact, and they agree to start on the provision, the Claimant will be referred to as a “Participant”

the term “Participant” is used in CSS1 this means the “Claimant” until they agree to join and are a start and therefore then a Participant

working days are defined as Monday to Friday and do not include Saturdays

1.18 The preference would be for Confident Futures meetings to be face to face, where it is possible to help with rapport building and offer practical support, but it will be driven by whichever form of contact is most comfortable for the Participant.

1.19 All Confident Futures provider guidance must be read in conjunction with:

the “Confident Futures Call-Off Specification”

your Terms and Conditions

your Contract

DWP IT Systems Provider Referrals and Payments (PRaP) User Guidance, and

DWP Supplier Code of Conduct

1.20 This guidance provides additional information to the schedules of your contract(s). provider guidance does not look to replicate or replace the details within your contract, and you are responsible for ensuring you read, understand and are complying with your contract.

1.21 You must ensure that any organisations with which you have a sub-contractual relationship also have access to, and have read, the Confident Future’s provider guidance.

1.22 If you have any questions which are not covered by this guidance, raise with your Employment Account Division Performance Manager (EAD PM) in the first instance.

Document retention

1.23 Providers must maintain complete documents and records in relation to Confident Futures for the period of their contract. The contract Terms & Conditions will set out the relevant contract periods and the Records Retention End Date.

Welsh Language Act

1.24 Providers are reminded of the need to comply with the provisions of Schedule 16 (Welsh Language) in providing the Services in the Welsh language. This must apply to all your staff and supply chain.

1.25 Details will be in the relevant schedules as set out within your contract.

The Employment Provision Provider Code of Conduct (“Code”)

1.26 The Code outlines the standards and behaviours that the government expects of all its providers when they are working with government, and how providers can help the government deliver for taxpayers.

1.27 Providers that contract with the DWP will be expected to operate in accordance with the Code. The Code can be found at Schedule 14 of the Confident Futures Agreement.

Obtaining a Participant signature

1.28 When obtaining a Participant’s signature, Confident Futures is not prescriptive about how the signature is obtained. You have the option to use one (or more) robust digital alternatives to obtain and store a Participant’s signature as part of the evidence of activities undertaken.

1.29 Participant signatures will continue to be monitored as part of the Performance Compliance Officer (PCO) Compliance Checking Regime.

1.30 If you are unable to obtain Participant signatures on any required forms, you must clearly demonstrate that all reasonable efforts were made to secure them. Ensure that each attempt is dated and recorded, with supporting evidence kept for compliance and assurance activity.

1.31 You are reminded to comply with UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and DWP security requirements when engaging in any digital delivery.

Digital technology

1.32 Providers are encouraged to use existing digital technology and explore the potential of new and emerging technologies, as part of the package of support they provide for Participants. This is both in terms of providing more choice over how the Participant engages with the provider and if appropriate, improving the digital skills of the Participant. This use should recognise the different needs of Participants and adhere to DWP’s confidentiality data sharing policies, security policies, and security standards.

1.33 The provider must be able to communicate with and receive communications from DWP in line with the DWP email policy. To note, use of technologies may require security risk assessment and Authority approval before commencement.

Confident Futures - General information

1.34 Confident Futures is designed for Claimants on the Universal Credit (UC) Health Journey who have had a Work Capability Assessment (WCA) and are assessed as having Limited Capability for Work and Work-Related Activity (LCWRA).

1.35 The provider of Confident Futures will provide a voluntary offer of personalised employment, health and skills support. The Programme will be informed by the social model of disability and will focus on building engagement and supporting Participants to increase their independence, confidence, motivation and self-belief, develop strategies to manage their health condition, improve their wellbeing, and engage in work-focused activity, helping them move towards employment or other DWP provision.

1.36 The provider shall design and deliver tailored interventions that reflect the diverse needs, characteristics, and circumstances of the Participant. Wraparound support will address multiple needs, such as finances, caring responsibilities, housing, addiction problems, debt and link the Participant to relevant specialist services: for example, housing, substance misuse, education and training providers.

1.37 Confident Futures provides a maximum of 365 calendar days of support to a Participant. Once a Participant has started on the provision, they should be offered a minimum of 182 calendar days of support. The duration of the support offer may be less than 182 calendar days in circumstances where the Participant exits the programme early.

1.38 The frequency of contact shall be Participant led, although there shall be meetings no less frequently than every 4 calendar weeks as a minimum. The provider shall offer meetings every 4 calendar weeks, face to face being the preference, or via an alternative method agreed with the Participant (for example, telephone or video call). Contact may take place more frequently as led by the Participant’s needs and preferences.

Overview of Confident Futures

1.39 Confident Futures is a voluntary programme providing personalised employment, health and skills support for disabled people and those with health conditions to make progress closer to and, where right for them, into work.

1.40 As part of supporting the Participant on Confident Futures you must deliver the following:

1. Initial engagement or assessment:

assign a Dedicated Adviser to each Participant. Each Dedicated Adviser will have a caseload consisting of no more than 25 Participants who are actively engaging with the support offer

participate in a Warm Handover call involving you, (wherever possible, this will be the Dedicated Adviser assigned to the Participant), the Pathways to Work Adviser (PTWA) and the Claimant

conduct an Initial Meeting with the Claimant within 15 working days of receiving the referral in PRaP

ensure any reasonable accessibility requirements are accommodated

complete a Needs Assessment with the Participant within 15 working days of the Initial Meeting and informed by the Needs Assessment, complete and finalise the Initial Support Plan within the same 15 working day period

2. On provision support

Dedicated Advisers meet with the Participant no less than every 4 calendar weeks and plan to deliver interventions more frequently than this to deliver the level of personalised quality support required.

prioritise face to face meetings, supported by a blended delivery approach based on Participant needs considering any reasonable adjustments or accessibility needs for full participation in the provision

where meetings are conducted face to face, an appropriate environment should be ensured, including privacy if appropriate

provide personalised employment, health and skills support for disabled people and those with health conditions to make progress closer to and, where right for them, into work

help Participants to devise strategies to support work-focussed activity alongside assisting them to understand and manage their health condition

provide wraparound support to address multiple needs (such as finances, caring responsibilities, and housing)

ensure Dedicated Advisers have access to appropriate health expertise

assess the extent of each Participant’s wider support network and collaborate with them to build a sustainable support structure that aligns with their needs

provide job search skills and career guidance, and link the Participant to local employment opportunities

provide job interview experience

provide advice on engaging employers and the workplace

utilise links to local services and community organisations to support each Participant to access relevant opportunities, including developing and maintaining relationships with employers and local stakeholders to source appropriate vacancies and work opportunities for each Participant who become ready to progress into work

broker volunteering opportunities for the Participant in order to carry out a period of work experience

work in partnership with local support service systems, including Local Authorities, health services and skills providers, to deliver integrated support and effectively address multiple needs

design and deliver a plan of tailored interventions which directly respond to the Participant’s individual needs, with a specific focus on increasing their self-reliance, self-belief and independence

provide specialist, non-clinical support to each Participant to support them to formulate strategies and solutions to a range of challenges, with the ultimate aim of engaging in work-focused activity

provide quality support through a flexible delivery model, including a variety of channels and local venues where possible, in response to each Participant’s needs and preferences

provide practical help such as travel assistance and covering childcare costs

3. In-Work Support (IWS)

where a Participant moves into work, offer and, if the Participant accepts, provide in‑work support, regular contact, including an offer of face to face meetings at least every 4 calendar weeks for either the remainder of their time on the programme (up to 365 days from their start date) or until the Participant no longer requires it

support will include practical assistance, and facilitation of reasonable adjustments (including Access to Work (AtW))

produce an Employment Support Plan (ESP) for those Participants in receipt of In-Work Support within 10 working days of the job starting

check the possible impact on the Participant’s welfare benefits of any paid employment undertaken and ensure these are understood by the Participant

4. Six-Month Touchpoint/Warm Handback

the PTWA will use the provider booking system to arrange the Touchpoint appointment

the Dedicated Adviser will complete a UCCF02 notification form at least 20 working days before day 182 for all active caseload Participant’s and send this to the designated Jobcentre Plus inbox, notified to you by DWP, unless the Participant is on a break. Refer to Chapter 3g Breaks in Support.

the Dedicated Adviser will lead the Six-Month Touchpoint with the Participant and their PTWA

the meeting should take place according to the channel preferred by the Participant (for example, face to face, telephone, or video call)

where the Participant’s preference is face to face, delivery may take place at a local Jobcentre Plus office (subject to local arrangements). The meeting shall be arranged by the PTWA at a time suitable to the Participant and provider, and they shall ensure that any accessibility requirements are met

use the Six-Month Touchpoint to determine if the Participant’s time as a Participant should continue beyond the initial 182 days. The final decision shall rest with the Participant

prior to the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting, you must discuss and prepare a Progress Report with the Participant, outlining progress achieved and agreeing the next steps

if the Participant decides to end their time and return to Jobcentre Plus support, this Touchpoint should act as a Warm Handback to the PTWA

ensure the Progress Report is available to the Participant at the end of their time on programme by including it as an addendum to the Support Plan. The Support Plan must then be updated and shared with the Participant within 10 working days of the Warm Handback meeting, including the agreed outcomes and next steps

1.41 All Claimants will be referred to you by the PTWA, who will have used the relevant criteria to identify eligible and suitable Participants for the provision.

1.42 Jobcentre Plus is the final decision maker for determining if an individual is eligible and suitable for the provision. Where eligibility concerns arise after referral, providers should take the actions set out in this guidance and notify Jobcentre Plus. Jobcentre Plus remains the final decision maker regarding eligibility and suitability.

Confident Futures Quick Start Guide

1.43 The table below shows a high-level overview of a Participant’s journey highlighting the minimum interactions that happen between the PTWA, Dedicated Adviser and Claimant/Participant.

Number High level steps Action Chapter ref

3 Warm Handover booking PTWA uses locally agreed arrangements to book a Warm Handover call with the provider. 2

4 Warm Handover call and Initial Meeting appointment PTWA, Claimant and provider attend the Warm Handover (wherever possible, this will be the Dedicated Adviser assigned to the Participant). The provider then books the Initial Meeting with the Claimant. 2

Providers required to meet 100% of this target. -

Who is Eligible to be Referred to Confident Futures

1.44 Claimants shall be referred by a PTWA on a voluntary basis and must fulfil the following eligibility and suitability criteria to be considered. The PTWA will determine eligibility and suitability.

1.45 The Claimant will be eligible for the provision if all the following criteria are met:

is on Universal Credit (UC) and has been assigned to the Limited Capability for Work-Related Activity (LCWRA) group

is not in any form of paid work, does not have a job offer or is not about to start work,

is not participating in any other supported employment programme funded by DWP

has not previously received Confident Futures support

is not in full-time education or training

has the right to work in the UK

resides in England or Wales

is of working age (18 to State Pension age in England, 16 to State Pension age in Wales)

Note: ‘not be in any form of paid work’, as stated in the second bullet above, also applies to self-employment. Potential Participants should not be in any form of employment (including, not employed, self-employed or on a zero-hours contract) when a referral is made.

Note: A Participant may be undertaking voluntary work and may be deemed to be suitable by their PTWA for Confident Futures.

1.46 Once eligible Claimants have been identified, a suitability check will be undertaken by the PTWA to ensure the provision is suitable for the Claimant based on their circumstances.

1.47 A Participant will become ineligible for the provision and must end their participation if they:

move outside of England or Wales for a period longer than 90 calendar days, or a period that is expected to be longer than the Participant’s remaining time on Confident Futures; or

receive a custodial sentence and are residing at His Majesty’s Prison for a period longer than 90 calendar days; or

no longer have the right to work or reside in the UK; or

die; or

move into full-time education or training; or

move into alternative DWP-funded provision

Suitability

1.48 The following criteria will be available to the PTWA to support the assessment of suitability.

1.49 A Claimant will be suitable for the provision if:

they think they could engage in work-focussed activity with the right support with a view to potentially securing work in the future, and

they are able to take advantage of the support (for instance their health condition means that they would be able to engage with the support offer)

1.50 Factors to consider when assessing a Claimant’s suitability are:

is the Claimant in a position to engage with the support offer for at least 90 calendar days in the next 182 calendar days? (for example, will planned treatment for their health condition prevent this?)

does the Claimant have a terminal illness? {this would not preclude the individual from participating but may affect the extent to which they are able to take advantage of the support offer)

is there another employment support programme that may be more appropriate?

Provider Referrals and Payments (PRaP)

1.51 Claimants identified as being eligible and suitable for Confident Futures will be referred to you by a PTWA. You will receive a referral from the Provider Referrals and Payments (PRaP) system. The PRaP system enables secure, automated exchanges of information about Participants referred to Contracted Employment Programmes (CEP) and payments from DWP to providers.

1.52 You must not work with any Claimant without a PRaP referral.

1.53 The PRaP system also provides DWP and providers with transparent data about the cost and performance of Contracted Employment Provision, supporting contract and performance management.

1.54 For more information and PRaP actions, see Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payment System for Confident Futures.

Provision duration

1.55 The maximum time the provider is required to support the Participant on provision is 365 calendar days. Once a Participant starts on provision, they remain on provision until they become a Completer or Early Completer.

1.56 As the Participant approaches 182 calendar days of support the Dedicated Adviser shall lead a Six-Month Touchpoint with the Participant and the PTWA to agree whether the Participant wants to continue on provision up to the maximum 365 calendar days.

Chapter 2: Joining Confident Futures

2.1 This chapter explains the actions that you will need to take once an eligible and suitable Claimant has been identified by the PTWA for referral to Confident Futures. It covers your roles and responsibilities at the Warm Handover and Initial Meeting.

Warm Handover – Overview

2.2 The PTWA is responsible for confirming a Claimant’s eligibility and suitability for Confident Futures. They will discuss the outcome with the Claimant and provide an overview of the provision, including the support available. They will also confirm the Claimant’s interest in starting the provision.

2.3 If the Claimant is eligible, suitable and interested, the PTWA will explain the next steps and seek the Claimant’s agreement to proceed, including booking a 3-way Warm Handover call.

2.4 For Claimants where English is not their first language and/or have communication needs (for example, hearing impaired) it is the PTWA’s responsibility to ensure appropriate communication methods (for example, translators) are available up to and including the Warm Handover. The Claimant may also be accompanied by a supporter on the call to facilitate effective communication and engagement.

2.5 You shall establish and maintain dedicated, pre-bookable 40-minute Confident Futures appointments. This can be (but is not restricted to):

an online tool

a list of available appointments

someone to book appointments

2.6 When booking the Warm Handover, the PTWA will share the following information:

customer name

National Insurance number

Note: The PTWA will provide the referring Jobcentre and their contact details when booking the Warm Handover meeting, where the provider’s booking system allows this information to be captured.

2.7 The PTWA will arrange a 10-minute pre-call with the Claimant, to prepare them for the Warm Handover call. This will be followed immediately by a 30‑minute three‑way Warm Handover call involving the PTWA, Claimant and yourself. An interpreter or any other support will also be included where required. Where possible your representative at the Warm Handover should be the Dedicated Adviser who will provide ongoing support to the Claimant throughout their time on the programme.

2.8 During the Warm Handover, the PTWA shall introduce the Claimant and provide relevant information to support the conversation. Information previously shared by the Claimant with the PTWA shall be used, with the Claimant’s consent, to reduce unnecessary repetition and ensure a more personalised and effective Warm Handover call. This may include details of any known disabilities, complex needs, vulnerabilities, and any other relevant circumstances that may support the Claimant’s engagement and progression.

2.9 The Warm Handover call is an opportunity to begin developing the relationship between you and the Claimant. Wherever possible, the Dedicated Adviser assigned to support the Claimant throughout their journey should represent you during the Warm Handover. You shall lead the call and ensure that the Claimant understands the Provision’s requirements, expectations, and next steps. The Claimant can raise any questions or concerns about the support they can expect from you. The focus of the call is on engagement to explain what tailored support they can expect to receive on Confident Futures, taking into consideration their health condition, disability, barriers to work, aspirations and skills.

2.10 Any accessibility or safeguarding requirements can be identified and addressed to support Claimants in attending meetings. You and the Claimant will agree the date, time and location/mode of the Initial Meeting. Wherever appropriate, face to face meetings will be prioritised to support effective relationship building, while maintaining a flexible, Participant led approach that offers a blended delivery model to meet individual needs.

2.11 If the Claimant agrees and wishes to proceed, the PTWA will initiate the referral immediately following the Warm Handover call and provide the Claimant with the Confident Futures marketing information supplied by you if not already done so as part of initial conversations. Refer to Chapter 7: Data and Information Sharing with DWP Marketing section for further information.

2.12 Prior to the Warm Handover, the PTWA and Claimant must agree the frequency and method of light touch contact that will be maintained during their time on Confident Futures, in line with the Participants requirements.

Warm Handover - provider actions

2.13 Depending upon which system you have set up, the PTWA will either phone your call centre or access your booking tool, and you must have processes in place to support these arrangements.

2.14 During the Warm Handover meeting you will:

explain how the Claimant can benefit from Confident Futures services

address any issues or concerns raised by the Claimant and discuss any reasonable adjustments with them

agree the date, time, mode and location (if face to face) of the Initial Meeting with the Claimant, where they confirm they are happy to proceed

discuss any complex needs or vulnerabilities that the Claimant has shared, so you know how best to support them, and make the necessary arrangements to accommodate their needs

advise that where the initial meeting is not face to face, an Induction pack can be shared electronically provided the Participant is able to access and retain a copy for their own use after they have completed support. The provider should also offer to send the Participant a hard copy by post, but it is acceptable for the Participant to receive and use a digital version only, where this is their preference. Electronic Participant signatures to evidence receipt of the induction pack are acceptable

2.15 The following Claimant information will be included in the subsequent Provider Referral and Payment System (PRaP) referral and should not be asked for by you during the Warm Handover:

the PTWA’s current office location

the name of the provision

the name and ID number of the provider

the Claimant’s:

National Insurance number

email address

telephone number

address

a marker will identify where a Claimant has a known disability/disabilities, complex needs or vulnerabilities. The referral will not contain any additional information, and you should use the marker to establish more information during the Initial Meeting. Refer to Chapter 3c: Supporting Participants with complex needs and additional support needs on Confident Futures for further information on sharing information

if the Claimant requires any childcare support during their participation on the provision

if the Claimant falls into any of the following disadvantaged groups: ex-offender, misuser of drugs, misuser of alcohol

2.16 You must identify any safeguarding needs from information shared during the Warm Handover and tailor their Initial Meeting engagement accordingly.

2.17 You must advise the Claimant what personal identification is required for the Initial Meeting.

2.18 After the Warm Handover you will check that a PRaP referral has been received and that all the information is accurate and then accept the referral. If you identify that incorrect information has been received, refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures for further information.

2.19 A Claimant cannot start on Confident Futures without a PRaP referral being received by you. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures for further information of what to do where a referral is not received.

2.20 Multi Agency Public Protection Arrangements (MAPPA) cases need to be managed via a specified process with restricted access. See further guidance on MAPPA processes in paragraph 2.24.

Following the Warm Handover - provider actions

2.21 The adviser actions:

check for receipt of the PRaP referral

confirm that it is a Confident Futures opportunity, if it is not then you must reject the referral and request a new referral via a UCCF02 form

verify that the Claimants details have been entered correctly on PRaP and that all information is accurate before accepting the referral. For any PRaP actions, refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures

if you have not received a PRaP referral refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures for further information of what to do

you must record all Initial Engagement Activity on your internal systems as part of the audit process. The Warm Handover is the first significant Engagement Activity and must be recorded

you should continue to try to engage with the Participant and enable their attendance up until day 15 of the CSS 1 target period and not input the DNA code before day 15

if the initial meeting is not held within 15 working days and no DNA code is entered in PRaP you may fail CSS 1. If the customer is still interested, you can still register a start within 40 calendar days of the referral date; after this, the referral will automatically close in PRaP. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures for further information

Note: If a PRaP referral is not received and the PTWA confirms that the Claimant does not wish to start, you are expected to delete any personal information you have been supplied with in line with DWP Data Protection Policy and GDPR.

Following the Warm Handover - PTWA actions

2.22 The PTWA will:

issue your marketing materials to the Claimant if not already done so as part of initial conversations

issue a notification letter for Confident Futures – detailing that the programme is voluntary

make a referral to you using DWP’s Information Technology (IT) system. This will result in a referral on the PRaP system

Contact between Warm Handover and the Initial Meeting - Provider

2.23 The Adviser will:

ensure that appropriate communication methods (for example translators) are available if required, so Claimants have full access to Confident Futures.

maintain contact with the Claimant to ensure ongoing engagement. This allows any changes in circumstances to be considered, such as:

health-related issues

receiving a job offer

changes to travel arrangements

changes to support needs

use the communication method agreed with the Claimant during the Warm Handover. Where appropriate, additional communication methods may be used to encourage attendance, including sending reminders in advance of the meeting.

ensure that, during any communication, the Claimant is reminded to bring ID to the Initial Meeting.

in exceptional circumstances where a Claimant provides information indicating they may no longer be eligible or suitable (for example, they are due to start work or have planned surgery with a recovery period exceeding 90 calendar days):

advise the Claimant to report the change of circumstances through their Universal Credit account, and

if the referral has not been acknowledged cancel the referral on PRaP using the relevant code in scenario table in Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payment System for Confident Futures

if the referral has been acknowledged, cancel the referral on PRaP using Did Not Start (DNS) referring to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payment System for Confident Futures scenario table and;

submit a UCCF02 form to the designated Jobcentre Plus inbox, notified to you by DWP, advising PTWA of the reason.

Note: This process must only be used where there is clear evidence that the Claimant no longer meets the eligibility criteria or is unable to engage with the programme.

Claimants with Multi Agency Public Protection Arrangements (MAPPA) Restrictions

2.24 If the Participant is subject to Multi Agency Public Protection Arrangements (MAPPA), as soon as possible after the Warm Handover, but before the initial face to face meeting, the MAPPA Single Point of Contact (SPoC) for Jobcentre Plus will contact the provider SPoC to discuss the restrictions that are in place for the Participant. There are exceptional circumstances when you may receive the MAPPA J Form, but this will only be for those occasions where the Jobcentre Plus MAPPA SPoC has sought the permission of the Responsible Authority/Lead Agency to share the MAPPA J with you. Where there is a need to share this information with you, the Jobcentre Plus MAPPA SPoC will inform you how and when this will be shared.

2.25 Should any restrictions impact on the appropriateness of the Initial face to face Meeting appointment it is your responsibility to reschedule this for a time and venue that does not conflict with the restrictions imposed on the Participant.

2.26 For all Participants subject to MAPPA restrictions you must ensure, prior to setting any Confident Futures activities, that the activity fully complies with these. You should continually assess all the Participant’s Confident Futures activities against the MAPPA restrictions throughout their time on the Confident Futures.

Employment prior to starting on Confident Futures

2.27 The PTWA will determine if a Claimant is in work or has a job offer prior to referral to Confident Futures. If they identify the Claimant is in any form of work at that point in time, they will not make a referral.

2.28 Where you identify that the Claimant is in employment at the point of referral or has secured employment between referral and the Initial Meeting, you should advise the Claimant to report the change of circumstances through their Universal Credit account, and you must cancel the referral on PRaP and:

if the referral has not been acknowledged cancel the referral on PRaP using the relevant code in scenario table in Chapter 8 Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures

if the referral has been acknowledged cancel the referral on PRaP using Did Not Start (DNS) (refer to the scenario table in Chapter 8 Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures) and

submit a UCCF02 notification form to the designated Jobcentre Plus inbox (as notified to you), advising the PTWA that the referral has been cancelled due to eligibility concerns. This process should only be used where the Claimant has provided clear information indicating that they no longer meet the programme eligibility criteria

Customer Service Standards

2.29 Confident Futures providers are required to deliver 3 Customer Service Standards, designed to ensure that all Participants receive a quality service during their time on Provision. The Customer Service Standard covered in this chapter is:

Description of Customer Service Standards System used for measurement and percentage of achievement to meet Customer Service Standards

Customer Service Standard 1 (CSS 1): Providers must ensure that an Initial Meeting is conducted with a Participant via their preferred channel of engagement; face to face, video, or phone and a Start/Did Not Start/Did Not Attend is recorded on ICT systems as a minimum: 95% of cases within 15 working days of the referral (date of referral is counted as day zero). Providers required to meet 100% of target.

Note: the term Participant is used in CSS 1 this means the claimant until they agree to join and are a start and therefore then a Participant.

Initial Meeting – Introduction

2.30 This section covers the things that you need to do at the Initial Meeting with your Claimant and the action that should be taken following the meeting to record a start on IT systems; and what to do if a Claimant does not attend or does not wish to start on Confident Futures following the Initial Meeting.

Initial Meeting – Information

2.31 You must hold the Initial Meeting with the Claimant within 15 working days of the date of referral through the Claimant’s preferred channel of engagement. The Initial Meeting must be delivered by your Dedicated Adviser. The status of the meeting should be recorded in line with CSS 1 as either:

Started

Did Not Start (DNS)

Did Not Attend (DNA)

Note: For the purposes of the CSS 1 the 15 working days is counted from the day following the creation of the referral The date of the referral is counted as day zero.

2.32 The meeting should be conducted via the Claimant’s preferred channel of engagement. Options should include face to face, video call or phone call. Face to face meetings should be offered at a location that is appropriate for the Claimant.

2.33 If the Claimant does not attend, then further meetings must be booked to achieve a start by 15 working days of referral. You should, through a fast, responsive and flexible appointment system, utilise a variety of communication methods and attempts to maximise the chance of the Claimant starting on provision. You should utilise the full 15 working days prior to inputting a DNA into PRaP. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures.

2.34 Before commencing the initial meeting, you must verify the claimant’s identity by confirming the Claimant ID and ensuring the individual present is the correct claimant. If the Claimant ID cannot be verified or is unavailable, the meeting must not proceed and should be rearranged, wherever possible within the CSS1 timescales.

2.35 You should consider additional safeguarding requirements to enable vulnerable Claimants to start on programme. Information should be available via the Warm Handover. For further information on safeguarding vulnerable Participants, see Chapter 3c: Supporting Participants with Complex Needs.

2.36 You must ensure that:

the Initial Meeting takes place within 15 working days from the date the Referral was made by the PTWA and

verify that the Claimants details have been entered correctly on PRaP and that all information is accurate before accepting the referral

2.37 the outcome of the Initial Meeting must be recorded on PRaP as soon as possible after the Initial Meeting has taken place. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures.

2.38 Where the initial meeting does not take place within 15 working days and you have not entered a DNA code in PRaP, you may fail to meet CSS 1. If the Claimant is still interested you may still engage with the Participant, however, note that you only have 40 calendar days from the Referral being made in which to register a start. Following this time, the line will automatically close in PRaP. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures.

Initial Meeting - Provider: Dedicated Adviser Actions

2.39 At the start of the Initial Meeting, you must check your Claimant’s identity to ensure that you are satisfied that the person you are engaging with is the correct person. To do this, you may decide to ask them to state, or physically provide, a combination of their personal information, that you feel provides appropriate security assurance to confirm identity, such as:

full name

address

National Insurance number

other information, such as details that were included within the original referral from DWP

details you hold in your records

other means of identification, such as a passport, driving licence, or utility bill may be provided

2.40 These should be recorded as seen and the reference/serial number of these documents noted but you must not retain copies.

2.41 You must also confirm that there has been no change in circumstances that affect the Claimants eligibility and suitability for Confident Futures. You will need to take the following actions.

Check that the Claimant:

is not in any type of paid work, does not have a job offer or is not about to start work,

is engaged on any other DWP-funded provision or has been supported by Confident Futures previously and

establish/confirm the Claimants preferred method of communication and

identify and take into account any complex needs and/or additional support requirements, see Chapter 3c: Supporting Participants with Complex Needs.

2.42 In exceptional circumstances, where a Claimant provides information that raises genuine concerns about their eligibility or suitability (for example, they are due to start work or have a planned surgery with a recovery period exceeding 90 calendar days), you should advise the Claimant to report the change of circumstances through their Universal Credit account where appropriate. You should then cancel the referral on PRaP using DNS and submit a UCCF02 form to the designated Jobcentre Plus inbox, advising the PTWA of the reason. This process must only be used where there is clear evidence that the Claimant no longer meets the eligibility criteria or is unable to engage with the programme. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment System for Confident Futures.

2.43 Once the Participant agrees to start Confident Futures you must ensure that you provide them with an Induction Pack in either hard copy, digital format or both, according to the Participant’s preference, for which you should obtain confirmation of receipt from your Participant. Electronic Participant signatures to evidence receipt are acceptable.

2.44 The Induction Pack should contain as a minimum:

your health and safety instructions

details of your responsibilities under Data Protection Legislation

travel and expenses declaration, childcare and other expenses, including any evidence your Participant will need to produce to enable them to make a successful claim for example, bus ticket. This is to be signed by the Participant (wet or electronic signature)

your complaint process

your location/contact details of the Dedicated Adviser

Participant attendance and appointment agreement

any other information relevant to the Participant

List is not exhaustive.

2.45 There is no expectation for the induction pack to be discussed in full during the Initial Meeting; only essential and relevant information needs to be covered.

2.46 You should remind your Participant that their length of time on Confident Futures can be up to 365 calendar days and that this programme has been designed to allow them to receive holistic, tailored support to help them to address any barriers, better manage health conditions and move closer towards their employment goals.

2.47 You shall advise the Participant that, if necessary, they may take agreed breaks totalling up to 90 calendar days.

2.48 You should clearly explain the purpose of the Needs Assessment to your Participant, outlining how their involvement is central to the process. Ensure they understand how sharing their needs, goals, and preferences will directly shape their Support Plan and help make sure the support provided is tailored to what matters most to them.

2.49 You should start to obtain information relevant to completion of the Needs Assessment at the Initial Meeting but may decide it is not appropriate to formally complete it at this stage. It must however be completed, with the Participant, within 15 working days of the Initial Meeting, in accordance with CSS 2. Refer to Chapter 3: Supporting Participants on Confident Futures for further information on the Needs Assessment.

2.50 You should also advise the Participant that you will start an Initial Support Plan, which will be developed using information gathered from the Needs Assessment. You are required to create and agree the Support Plan with direct Participant input and finalise within 15 working days of the provider’s Initial Meeting with the Participant, in accordance with CSS 2. Refer to provider guidance Chapter 3: Supporting Participants on Confident Futures for more information about the Support Plan.

2.51 Prior to ending the meeting, you must discuss your future contact and engagement arrangements with your Participant, along with the date, time and location/mode of their next meeting with you.

2.52 If the Participant agrees that the next meeting is face to face, the location must be within 90 minutes of travel from the Participant’s home address. Where a Participant’s health condition limits their ability to travel, you are expected to make appropriate arrangements to meet the Participant, for example at outreach locations.

2.53 If the next meeting is not face to face you will need to explain how that meeting will take place such as via video call, or phone call.

2.54 For all Participants identify and take into account any health conditions, disabilities, complex needs and/or additional support requirements. Refer to Chapter 3c: Supporting Participants whilst on Confident Futures for more information.

Following the Initial Meeting – Provider Dedicated Adviser Actions

2.55 Following the completion of the Initial Meeting you must:

record the date of the meeting on your own internal Systems and in the PRaP system, see Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payments System for Confident Futures, and the section covering recording a Start

record and retain evidence of the Start Date which will be required to be produced during PCO checks, see Chapter 9: Contract and Managing Performance. Examples of acceptable evidence could include, but are not limited to:

induction pack items that have been signed for

site attendance register

if a face to face Initial Meeting did not take place, then digital evidence could include, but not limited to, a dated electronic receipt from the Participant

Claimant Does Not Attend/Does Not Start Initial Meeting – Provider actions

2.56 You must aim to carry out an Initial Meeting and achieve a Participant Start Date within 15 working days of the Referral in line with CSS 1 target timescale. If the Claimant fails to attend their Initial Meeting, you shall continue to make attempts to engage with them using the communication method previously agreed at the Warm Handover. To support this, you must operate a fast, responsive and flexible appointment system and utilise a variety of communication methods to maximise engagement and enable the Claimant to attend their Initial Meeting and start on provision within the required timescale.

2.57 You must attempt to understand the reason for the missed meeting and use this information to inform ongoing engagement. This may include identifying and working around any challenges the Claimant may face to help them engage.

2.58 You must utilise the full 15 working days prior to recording a Did Not Attend (DNA) in PRaP. A DNA must only be recorded where you have been unable to make contact with the Claimant within this period. If the Claimant makes contact to rearrange their appointment, you shall rearrange the appointment, noting that the CSS 1 timescale will still apply.

2.59 Once you have input the DNA code into PRaP the PTWA will follow up with the Claimant about the missed appointment and discuss whether a referral to the programme is still appropriate. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payments System.

2.60 Where a Claimant attends their Initial Meeting but decides not to continue on provision, a Did Not Start (DNS) should be entered on PRaP by you as the outcome of the Initial Meeting. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payments System.

2.61 A Claimant can be considered for re-referral, following a DNA/DNS subject to their PTWA’s re-assessment on whether a re-referral is the most suitable option. A re-referral cannot be considered in any circumstance after a Participant has formally started on provision.

2.62 If a Start, DNS or DNA have not been recorded and the Claimant has not started on the Provision after 40 calendar days from the date of the Referral, PRaP will auto-cancel the Referral.

Inappropriate referrals

2.63 A referral may be regarded as inappropriate where an error is identified after the Referral has been made on PRaP by the PTWA but prior to the date of the Initial Meeting. In such cases, you shall:

if the referral has not been acknowledged, reject the referral on PRaP using the relevant scenario code table in Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payments System

if the referral has been acknowledged, cancel the referral on PRaP using Did Not Start (DNS) (refer to the scenario table in Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referrals and Payments System)

the Provider must send a UCCF02 notification form to the designated in box to notify of the reason for cancellation. Further information is set out in Chapter 8

Duplicate Referrals

2.64 Where a Duplicate Referral has been identified, you should:

where you identify a duplicate referral, you must immediately contact PRaP Operational, Digital and Database Support (PODDS) with the Participant’s Purchase Order (PO) number

if the duplicate is identified before you have acknowledged the referral you can take action to reject it and follow the process of rejecting the referral

if the Participant has already been on Confident Futures, and you have claimed a start, you must cease working with the Participant and initiate the PRaP 14 process

once identified, you will be advised as to the PO number requiring a PRaP 14 request to be raised in order to remove the start line. Once the action has been completed by PODDS, you must cancel the referral and claim Did not Start

2.65 Guidance on the process for the correct action to be taken and the rejection reason can be found in Chapter 8 Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures.

Chapter 3: Supporting Participants on Confident Futures

3.1 This chapter covers the ongoing engagement you will undertake and the holistic, tailored support you will provide, enabling you to deliver the best possible outcomes for your Participants throughout their journey on Confident Futures.

Customer Service Standards

3.2 Confident Futures providers are required to deliver 3 Customer Service Standards, designed to ensure that all Participants receive a quality service. The Customer Service Standards covered in this chapter are:

Description of Customer Service Standards System used for measurement and percentage of achievement to meet Customer Service Standards

Customer Service Standard 2 (CSS 2): The Supplier shall start an Initial Support Plan with the Participant at the Initial Meeting and finalise this Initial Support Plan within 15 working days of that meeting, informed by a Needs Assessment and information shared at the Warm Handover meeting. DWP IT systems and PCO checks will provide assurance. For 97% of Participants who start the programme.

Customer Service Standard 3 (CSS 3): The Supplier shall ensure that the Dedicated Adviser leads a Six-Month Touchpoint meeting in respect of each Participant except those Participants who are no longer UC Claimants. The Six-Month Touchpoint meeting shall be attended by the Dedicated Adviser, the Participant and the Pathways to Work Adviser. The Supplier shall ensure that, within 10 working days of the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting being completed: (1) the Support Plan is updated and (2) the outcome and agreed next steps from the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting are captured and shared with the Participant. DWP IT systems and PCO checks will provide assurance. For 100% of active Participants

Support for Confident Futures Participants

Tailored support

3.3 The Dedicated Adviser should work closely with the Participant to build a trusted relationship and develop a thorough understanding of their individual circumstances, needs, barriers, and aspirations. They should help the Participant receive the right support at the right time, either through direct delivery or by sourcing, coordinating, and securing access to specialist services and interventions where these are better placed to meet the Participant’s needs.

3.4 Participants should receive tailored, personalised, and holistic support that reflects their individual circumstances and helps them address multiple and complex barriers to employment. This support may include, but is not limited to:

support to manage health conditions and/or disabilities, including peer networks and helping Participants develop strategies to balance work-focused activity with effective management of their health condition

building confidence, resilience, and self-belief

skills development to support progression towards and into employment

wraparound support to address wider barriers, including financial difficulties, caring responsibilities, housing needs, and other factors that may affect a Participant’s ability to move towards work

navigation and advocacy support: to help Participants identify, access, and engage with local services, including accompanying Participants to appointments where this is necessary to overcome barriers to engagement and achieve agreed outcomes

3.5 To facilitate delivery of a comprehensive and intensive support offer, the Participant should be offered regular face to face engagement meetings, no less than every 4 calendar weeks. This is to facilitate rapport building and offer practical support, but the method of contact will be driven by whichever form of contact is preferred for by the Participant. You shall ensure that contact is meaningful, clearly addressing barriers to work and helping to progress the Participant.

3.6 You shall ensure that all premises used for the delivery of the Provision are reasonably and readily accessible to Participants, including Participants who rely on public transport.

3.7 Where a Participant agrees to attend meetings at your premises or an outreach location, you shall ensure that the Participant is able to travel to and from relevant premises by public transport and that, having regard to the Participant’s individual circumstances, the journey shall not exceed 90 minutes in each direction, using an appropriate route and means of transport.

3.8 Where a Participant’s health condition limits their ability to travel, you are expected to make appropriate arrangements to meet the Participant, for example at outreach locations.

3.9 You shall have flexibility in determining the method of delivery for face to face meetings in such locations, provided that the Services remain accessible to the Participant and they are offered in an appropriate location.

3.10 Where face to face meetings do occur, you shall bear any associated costs that the Participant incurs.

3.11 Meetings can be supplemented with contact via text message or email, but this should not be the primary method of engagement unless specifically requested by the Participant for example as part of the light touch support during breaks.

3.12 Where a Participant is on an arranged break, light-touch support and contact can be maintained, in accordance with arrangements made with the Participant in advance.

3.13 You are responsible for ensuring that you are able to evidence all meetings, along with any other engagement meetings with your Participant that you deem necessary. The type of evidence may include but is not limited to:

signed attendance registers

electronic confirmation from your Participant

signed Participant Support Plan

3.14 This support must include, but is not limited to, the following:

regular engagement meetings no less than every 4 calendar weeks which could be face to face by phone or digital. Face to face is the preferred method of engagement

the Support Plan should be reviewed at each engagement meeting to demonstrate a record of continuous support relevant to the Participants needs and goals and act as a record of progression for the Participant

the Needs Assessment should be reviewed every 90 calendar days to ensure support remains relevant to the Participant and clearly show progress towards or completion of requirements

In-Work Support which will include an Employment Support Plan being produced within 10 working days of employment commencing

light touch support during breaks (if requested) ensure that contact is meaningful, clearly addressing barriers to work and helping to progress the Participant. Communication via text message(s) and/or emails will not suffice unless specifically requested by the Participant for example as part of the light touch support during breaks

3.15 You should also ensure that your internal systems are updated to show the details of the meetings which take place and that any reason for non-attendance is also recorded.

3.16 Should your Participant not wish to meet as frequently as every 4 calendar weeks due to personal circumstances this should be clearly detailed on your internal systems and within their Support Plan. The suitability of continuing support should be discussed with the Participant and reviewed regularly, taking account of their needs and preferences. The Dedicated Adviser should, where possible, maintain contact via text and/or email in line with the Participant’s preferred method of communication considering Participants’ needs and preferences.

3.17 When working with Participants, you should tailor engagement meetings to take into account:

local employment growth and training initiatives where suitable/appropriate

local support services

health support

3.18 You should ensure that the Adviser maintains an Active Caseload of up to 1:25 to ensure they have sufficient time to deliver quality support to each Participant, including those in work who wish to remain on Provision. Inactive Participants will remain part of the Total Caseload until formally classified as Disengaged.

3.19 Caseload sizes will be regularly reviewed as part of the DWPs Performance Management Regime as detailed in Chapter 9: Contract and Managing Performance. Where the Active Caseload falls below 1:25, we will work with you to refer additional Participants onto the Provision.

3.20 Caseload referenced within this provider guidance relates exclusively to Confident Futures Participants and must not be combined with any other customer caseloads.

3.21 Throughout your Participant’s time spent on Confident Futures you must ensure that they are aware of, and clearly understand any potential implications of, any paid employment and self-employment on benefits that they may be in receipt of.

3.22 You should support and encourage your Participant to utilise the independent benefits calculators through Benefits calculators so that your Participant can make an informed decision and understand the effect of any earnings if they start work or increase their earnings.

3.23 You should ensure, wherever possible, that the meeting is face to face when you are supporting Participants to use benefits calculators. If they are not present, you must ensure they clearly understand that calculations depend on the accuracy of the information provided and are not guaranteed. You must ensure the Participant reads and understands the disclaimer included within the online benefits calculator.

3.24 You may also find it helpful to signpost Participants to the Government’s Right to Try guidance, as it reassures eligible benefit claimants that taking up work or volunteering will not, in itself, trigger a reassessment of their benefit award. The policy is designed to give people with disabilities or long-term health conditions greater confidence to test their ability to work in a safe and predictable way, helping to reduce concerns that engaging with employment opportunities could automatically affect their benefits.

Needs Assessment

3.25 You must complete a Needs Assessment within 15 working days of your Initial Meeting with the Participant to inform their Support Plan, in accordance with CSS 2.

3.26 Information relevant to the completion of the Needs Assessment must begin to be gathered at the Initial Meeting, although it may not be appropriate to formally complete the Needs Assessment during that meeting. The Needs Assessment should be a key focus and, should be completed by the Dedicated Adviser assigned to the Participant. This will help establish a trusted relationship from the outset of the Participant’s time on Confident Futures.

3.27 The Needs Assessment should establish the Participant’s circumstances, support requirements and aspirations, and identify barriers to engaging in work-focused activity and employment. It should also identify the resources and support required to help the Participant progress towards their goals.

3.28 Areas of focus may include, but are not limited to:

gaps in job-related skills

health conditions and disabilities

self-belief and confidence

housing issues and personal debt

work-related independence skills, such as mobility and the ability to travel independently

attitudes towards work and aspirations for future employment

current support networks

existing skills, interests and hobbies that may support future employment opportunities

previous work experience, training and qualifications

3.29 The Needs Assessment is a fundamental step in the Participant’s journey towards employment and should support the development of a positive working relationship between you and the Participant. Understanding each Participant’s aspirations, needs and challenges will enable support and activities to be tailored to their individual circumstances.

3.30 You should deliver the Needs Assessment in a way that promotes trust, openness and Participant engagement. The assessment should help Participants reflect on their circumstances and identify their needs and aspirations, enabling the development of tailored and effective support. Participant needs should continue to be identified and reviewed through ongoing discussions and formal reviews of the Needs Assessment.

3.31 You are responsible for designing a customer-centred Needs Assessment that is capable of capturing all information necessary to inform the Support Plan.

3.32 As the programme supports individuals with multiple barriers and complex needs, you must be able to evidence a clear process for identifying and assessing factors that may affect a Participant’s progression towards employment. Examples may include:

advocacy support, for example in relation to debt or housing issues

signposting to local initiatives and support services

advice on coping strategies for particular health conditions

support through significant life-changing events

3.33 The Needs Assessment must be reviewed with the Participant at least every 90 calendar days to ensure that support remains relevant and continues to reflect their circumstances and to ensure that progress is being made towards, or requirements have been completed in line with the Participant’s agreed support activities and goals.

3.34 The review must capture any changes that may positively or negatively affect progression towards employment, including safeguarding concerns, changes in circumstances, emerging barriers and additional support needs.

3.35 Any changes identified through the review must be reflected in the Participant’s Support Plan.

Initial Support Plan and Support Plan

3.36 The first version of the Support Plan is the Initial Support Plan, once completed, the Initial Support Plan becomes the Participant’s live Support Plan and should be updated as required throughout their participation to ensure it remains current and relevant.

3.37 The Initial Support Plan must be informed by the Needs Assessment and set out the support and actions required to help the Participant achieve one or more goals. It should reflect the Participant’s circumstances, needs, barriers, goals and aspirations at the time it is developed.

3.38 The Initial Support Plan shall be signed, by wet or electronic signature, and dated by the Participant and Dedicated Adviser on the day of the Initial Meeting and shall be finalised within 15 working days of that meeting, in accordance with CSS 2.

3.39 You shall consult and work with the Participant’s support network, which could include family, carers, or social workers, in order to help complete the Initial Support Plan and maintain and update the Support Plan throughout delivery of support. You shall obtain their contact information from the Participant, who will not be obligated to share these details unless and they agree with the Participant that their information can be shared. If agreement is in place, you shall consult the support network through any available means such as face to face, telephone call or video call. For the avoidance of doubt, any associated costs shall be included within the Confident Futures Delivery Fee.

3.40 When sharing personal data with a Participant’s support network, you must comply with UK GDPR and all other applicable data protection legislation and obtain and record the Participant’s consent before any such sharing. If consent is not provided, or is subsequently withdrawn, you must not share the Participant’s personal data with their support network.

3.41 The Initial Support Plan shall include, as a minimum, the required information to commence support:

the date and time of the next meeting, or contact

the location/mode of the next meeting

the Participant’s preferred method of communication

any action to take in preparation for the next meeting; for example, a list of the Participants’ support network or other action to be agreed (if shared)

any further adjustments or support required

offer of 4 weekly support

3.42 The Support Plan should translate the findings of the Needs Assessment into a structured programme of support, activities and actions designed to address identified barriers and help the Participant achieve their agreed goals.

3.43 As the Provision will support Participants with complex needs, the Supplier shall demonstrate a clearly defined process to identify and assess the impact of a wide range of factors which may affect the Participant’s employability and identify and/or provide the support to address these. These may include:

physical and mental health conditions

confidence, motivation and wellbeing

housing, debt and other financial circumstances

significant life-changing events

social and personal barriers to employment

access to local support services and community networks

any other circumstances that may affect a Participant’s ability to move towards or sustain employment

3.44 The Support Plan should clearly record:

the Participant’s views and perspectives

identified needs, barriers and goals

agreed support, activities and actions

how planned support will address the needs identified through the Needs Assessment

3.45 Activities recorded in the Support Plan may include, but are not limited to:

supporting the Participant to build confidence and develop strategies to manage their health condition, including through peer support networks

supporting the Participant to engage in work-focused activities

helping the Participant to address social and personal barriers to employment, such as housing issues

engaging with relevant networks, charities, advocates and other sources of support

3.46 The Support Plan shall be updated regularly, including when the Needs Assessment is updated, to ensure it accurately reflects the Participant’s current support needs.

3.47 The Support Plan shall:

set out clear aims and achievable targets that support progression towards employment

include interventions to address identified barriers, including those relating to health, mobility, wellbeing and financial security

detail the agreed type and frequency of Participant contact, including any circumstances where the Participant chooses not to engage with the minimum expectation of 4-weekly meetings

describe the support required to address the Participant’s needs and barriers

demonstrate how the provider will strengthen the Participant’s support networks

explain how agreed activities contribute to the Participant’s progression and milestones

3.48 Where support is provided by more than one organisation, including subcontractors or external partners, you must ensure all contributions are recorded within the Support Plan.

3.49 The Support Plan must describe all support that the Participant is accessing or is due to access, including support delivered by you and any Non-Confident Futures Activities. Each activity must be recorded separately, include the relevant delivery period, and specify the amount of time to be spent on that activity, including any Non-Confident Futures Activity.

3.50 You shall ensure that each Participant has access to a single, up-to-date Support Plan that is made available in an electronic and/or hard copy format appropriate to their needs, disabilities and health conditions. The Support Plan shall, as a minimum, include:

a description of the services you are providing to the Participant

any actions required of the Participant in relation to the services

all non-Confident Futures activities

3.51 The Support Plan is a living document and must be updated at each meeting to reflect agreed actions and changes in circumstances. As a minimum, the Support Plan must be reviewed and updated every 4 calendar weeks and whenever changes identified through a Needs Assessment review affect the Participant’s support requirements.

3.52 You must obtain both Participant and your signatures, wet or electronic, on the Support Plan whenever it is updated. Participants must be provided with a copy of the signed Support Plan, in an accessible format, following each update.

3.53 You must retain all versions of the Support Plan throughout the Participant’s time on provision and for the duration of the Contract for audit and compliance purposes.

3.54 You shall update the Support Plan with a Progress Report at the Six-Month Touchpoint and the Warm Handback. Further requirements relating to Progress Reports are set out in the Progress Report section.

Unsuitable types of activity

3.55 Participants must not be helped to engage in activities, including starting businesses which could put them at risk or bring DWP or you as a provider into disrepute. It would be difficult to produce an exhaustive list of unsuitable activities. However, Participants subjected to Multi Agency Public Protection Arrangements (MAPPA) restrictions must not be helped into activities that breach these.

3.56 You should also take into account your Participant’s personal beliefs when identifying job or training opportunities, for example, some individuals may have personal or religious beliefs about working in certain industries or on certain days, and you should be sensitive to these.

Six-Month Touchpoint

3.57 The Dedicated Adviser shall lead a 40-minute Six-Month Touchpoint meeting with all active Participants, for whom a Six-Month Touchpoint is required, and PTWA. This will be held either on day 182 from the Participant’s start date on the programme, or within 20 working days of this date. The provider shall notify the PTWA 20 working days before day 182 of the requirement for a Six-Month Touchpoint meeting by emailing the notification form UCCF02 to the PTWA, via the designated Jobcentre Plus in box, who will arrange the meeting using your booking tool within 15 working days of receipt of the form.

3.58 The meeting shall be conducted via the Participant’s preferred channel of engagement (for example in-person, phone call, or video call) with the Authority’s preference being for face to face delivery at a local Jobcentre Plus (subject to local arrangements). Any reasonable accessibility requirements must be accommodated. The Six-Month Touchpoint meeting should be held on day 182 of the Participant’s start on provision, or within 20 working days of this date, but may be held later if a Participant is on a break (see below), or exceptionally, within the 20 working days before day 182 if this is more convenient for the Participant.

3.59 The purpose of the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting shall be to review the Participant’s progress and for the Participant to decide whether to continue the Provision. The final decision shall rest with the Participant. If the Participant is on a break at the 6-month point, the provider shall notify the PTWA of this using form UCCF02, and 20 working days before the end date of the break, contact the PTWA using form UCCF02 to request a 3-way call to review the Participant’s progress and decide whether they wish to continue on provision. The PTWA will arrange this meeting within 15 working days of receipt of the notification.

3.60 If the Participant fails to attend their Six-Month Touchpoint meeting, but has been engaged up to that point, the Dedicated Adviser will attempt to contact the Participant within 1 working day of the failure to attend. If they agree a new date and time with the Participant, the Dedicated Adviser will notify the PTWA, via the designated Jobcentre Plus in box, of this using notification form UCCF02. The PTWA will re-arrange the meeting within 15 working days of this notification.

3.61 If the Dedicated Adviser fails to contact the Participant within one working day of their failure to attend the meeting, they shall note their attempts at contact on the Participant’s Support Plan and begin the disengagement process. You shall attempt to contact the Participant daily, at different times of day, over 5 working days, taking into account what is reasonable and, proportionate to the Participant’s circumstances as set out in their Support Plan.

3.62 The Dedicated Adviser shall then attempt to make contact with the Participant once every 5 working days for the next 15 working days. You shall record on the Participant’s Support Plan the method(s) of communication used to contact the Participant, the date(s) and time(s) of attempted contact.

3.63 If contact is re-established, you should discuss the reasons for non-contact. If the Participant confirms that they no longer wish to continue on the programme, notify the PTWA, via the designated Jobcentre Plus in box, of this using notification form UCCF02, and take the required action on PRAP to end the Participants time on programme. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures and refer to end codes. If the Participant wishes to continue on the programme, notify the PTWA using the notification form, UCCF02 to arrange the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting, which they will arrange within 15 working days of receipt of the form.

3.64 Exceptionally, the Participant may confirm to you that they wish to continue their participation on the programme beyond day 182, but do not want to take part in a Six-Month Touchpoint meeting. You should encourage the Participant to take part in the Touchpoint and remind them that it is designed to support their ongoing needs. If they still do not wish to participate, note this and their reasons on the Support Plan, and notify the PTWA using the UCCF02 notification form that a Six-Month Touchpoint meeting will not be required, and the Participant will be continuing on provision.

3.65 If the Participant decides to end their time on the Provision and return to Jobcentre Plus support, the Six-Month Touchpoint should act as a Warm Handback to the PTWA.

3.66 The Support Plan must be updated and the outcome and agreed next steps captured and shared with the Participant within 10 working days of the Six-Month Touchpoint being complete, in line with CSS 3.

3.67 Where a Participant’s Universal Credit claim ends before they reach the point at which a Six-Month Touchpoint would normally be arranged, the Six-Month Touchpoint process set out in the Specification and this guidance will not apply, and there will be no requirement to send the UCCF02 notification form to Jobcentre Plus.

3.68 At the point that a Six-Month Touchpoint would normally be carried out, you may undertake a structured review of the Participant’s progress, ongoing support needs and future goals and record the outcome within the Support Plan, including confirming that the Participant wishes to continue receiving support on Confident Futures up to day 365. All other Confident Futures delivery, record-keeping, performance management and contractual reporting requirements remain unchanged.

Chapter 3a: Referring Participants to Additional Support Provision

3.69 Confident Futures is a specific stage within a wider, holistic support pathway: from identification and assessment, through targeted confidence and capability-building support, to onward progression for some into work-focussed activity and support offers such as Connect to Work, for other Participants, employment.

3.70 You shall help Participants to access other relevant services for which they are eligible so that the Confident Futures Services are experienced as part of a coherent package of support. When Participants are referred to other services, you shall ensure an effective exchange of information to help deliver a seamless service to the Participant.
