Any exchange must be in accordance with the Data Protection Act 2018 and the UK GDPR.

3.71 A Participant cannot receive support through both Confident Futures and another DWP-funded employment support programme concurrently. Where the provider becomes aware that a Participant has been referred to or started on Connect to Work, they should notify the PTWA (using UCCF02 notification form) so that the most appropriate support can be agreed.

3.72 Where a Participant has support needs which are above and beyond those that will be addressed by Confident Futures, additional provision may be considered. The decision to refer a Confident Futures Participant to additional provision should be made jointly with the Participant; it must be deemed to be in their best interest and not in any way affect their ability to participate fully in Confident Futures.

3.73 Where individual needs are identified, consideration may be given to sourcing appropriate additional support outside of Confident Futures to best meet the Participant’s requirements.

3.74 There is a wide range of provision available to Participants, both nationally and locally, to help them obtain the skills and experience they need to start work, gain more work or better paid work. This provision can be organised into 4 main types of support:

DWP-funded employment support programme: A Participant on Confident Futures cannot be referred to any additional DWP Contracted Employment Provision. It is the responsibility of Confident Futures provider to source and fund all appropriate mental health support for Participants who require it whilst on this programme, however Access to Work (AtW) and AtW Mental Health Support Service (MHSS) can be used to support someone in employment

Additional Provision delivered as part of Jobcentre Plus Offer: A Participant on Confident Futures cannot usually be referred to provision that is delivered as part of Jobcentre Plus Offer. This includes Sector Based Work Academy Programme (SWAP) which are not compatible with Confident Futures

a work experience opportunity subsidised or funded by you, or through an arrangement that you have with an employer or training partner (outside of the official SWAPs initiative) would be compatible with Confident Futures and could be considered for a Participant

non-DWP Contracted Provision: Provision offered by Local Authorities, Charities, the Private sector (this list is not exhaustive) may be compatible with Confident Futures. It is the responsibility of the provider to check the eligibility and suitability criteria of the specific provision or support being considered

Chapter 3b: Residency Tests and Participants with EU Settlement Scheme (EUSS) status

Participants and Residency Tests

3.75 You may be informed through a change of circumstances notification UCCF01, or by your Participant that they have an issue with their residency. If your Participant informs you of this, you may wish to contact the PTWA through a UCCF02 notification form to request a 2 or 3-way call to seek confirmation.

EUSS Status and Habitual Residence Test Decisions

3.76 Should your Participant fail the Habitual Residency Test (HRT), their Universal Credit claim will close. They will however remain on Confident Futures if they wish to do so and have the right to work and reside in the UK. Passing the Universal Credit HRT is not a requirement for continued participation where the individual retains the right to work and reside in the UK.

3.77 Should your Participant make a new claim for Universal Credit, they will remain a Participant until a new HRT is undertaken. Should your Participant pass the new HRT, the Participant will continue on the Confident Futures Programme. Should your Participant fail the new HRT but retains the right to work and right to reside in the UK, they may continue on Confident Futures if they wish to do so.

3.78 Should a Participant appeal an HRT decision that is subsequently overturned, their Universal Credit claim may be reinstated, they will be able to continue on the Confident Futures Programme.

3.79 You should be aware that the HRT used for Universal Credit assesses whether an individual is habitually resident in the UK and, where applicable, whether they have a qualifying right to reside for benefit purposes. A person’s right to work and general right to reside is determined by their immigration status, which the Home Office is responsible for. Support may continue to be provided to Participants who do not satisfy the HRT, but who hold Settled Status, Pre-Settled Status or a valid Certificate of Application under the EU Settlement Scheme. Providers should check and record the Participant’s right to work and general right to reside where appropriate.

Participants requiring permission to enter or remain in the UK

3.80 If a Participant’s leave to enter or remain in the UK expires whilst they are on Confident Futures, Jobcentre Plus will confirm the Participant’s immigration status via a UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form which will also provide the actions for you to take in all circumstances.

3.81 If Jobcentre Plus confirm that a Participant is an overstayer because they no longer hold valid leave and do not benefit from section 3C leave, they do not have permission to work in the UK. The Participant must be exited from Confident Futures using the appropriate Leaver Code.

3.82 If Jobcentre Plus confirm that the Participant made a valid application to the Home Office before their existing leave expired, their leave may be automatically extended under section 3C of the Immigration Act 1971 pending the outcome of that application. The Participant remains eligible for Confident Futures while they continue to hold valid leave. If leave is subsequently refused and no further entitlement to remain exists, they must be excited from Confident Futures using the appropriate Leaver Code.

Chapter 3c: Supporting Participants with complex needs and additional support needs on Confident Futures

Supporting Participants with complex needs

3.83 Complex needs may be defined as difficult personal circumstances or life events. They may be permanent or temporary in nature and the degree to which they affect a Participant will vary from one to another.

3.84 There is no prescriptive list of complex needs which DWP can supply. Some Participants will have obvious physical conditions which mean they need extra support or that adjustments are required to enable them to fully engage and access support fully. Other Participants may have conditions that are less obvious. You should refer to your organisations policies and guidance for further information regarding identification.

3.85 Examples of complex needs may include (but are not limited to):

learning disability

recent care leaver

drug or alcohol dependency

unable to read or write

homelessness

3.86 As a minimum you are expected to assess your Participants during every interaction, supported by information from Jobcentre Plus to identify complex needs and provide a support offer that is tailored to meet these needs where appropriate. This includes the activities you agree to support them to find and retain work.

3.87 Discussions with your Participant will encourage them to divulge more detail about their circumstances and enable them to agree the nature and extent of additional support you can offer, whilst ensuring those who feel capable of managing without the need for further support do not feel compelled to accept additional support. You may wish to make use of 3-way conversations to involve your Participant’s PTWA to share and verify information.

3.88 Support may be appropriate in the short, medium or long term. Discussions will also enable you to review the support you are providing if your Participant’s needs change. This includes where you both agree adjustments are no longer needed.

3.89 Confident Futures has been designed to suit Participants with a range of needs including health conditions and/or disabilities and related complex barriers to work including those with communication needs and/or complex needs. You are expected to make reasonable adjustments to help support these Participants whilst on Confident Futures.

3.90 DWP and its contracted providers have a legal duty to enable communication with Participants who do not speak English as a first language and/or require tailored support in response to their complex needs.

3.91 Claimants may be referred to the Confident Futures provision with a variety of complex needs or may develop them during their time on provision.

3.92 You must deliver support in response to these needs throughout a Participant’s time on provision. You must continually monitor their interaction, assess information from Jobcentre Plus and, where necessary, adapt your approach to ensure clear appropriate support is in place.

3.93 For further information on working with Participants with communication and/or complex needs, see Chapter 3c: Supporting Participants whilst on Confident Futures.

Sharing information regarding Participants with a disability, complex needs and/or vulnerabilities

3.94 The PTWA shall initiate a referral, and you will then receive a notification via a marker in PRaP where a Claimant has a known disability/disabilities, complex needs or vulnerabilities. The PRaP referral will not contain any additional information; you shall use the marker to establish more information during initial Claimant engagement.

3.95 Where a Participant has a known disability/disabilities, complex needs or vulnerabilities, this information shall also be shared during the Warm Handover between the Claimant, PTWA and Dedicated Adviser at the Claimants discretion.

3.96 A Participant may also develop a disability, complex needs and/or vulnerability during their time on programme. Where safeguarding issues are identified and action is undertaken. You will notify the PTWA, via the designated Jobcentre Plus in box, within one working day, by using notification form UCCF02 to request a 2-way or 3-way call, so both parties are up-to-date and providing appropriate aligned support. The subject line in the email should read as urgent.

3.97 On receipt of the UCCF02 notification form the PTWA will arrange the call in the same way they book the Warm Handover. The Participant does not have to be present at any such call. The call may be arranged at their request to either you or the PTWA.

3.98 You shall utilise appropriate communication routes, including 2 or 3-way conversations between yourself, PTWA and Participant where necessary, to enable the secure sharing of sensitive information, taking into account safeguarding requirements and any impact on participation in the Provision. Two and 3-way conversations shall be available throughout a Participant’s time on Provision via the submission of the UCCF02 form to the PTWA.

3.99 An alternative to 2 and 3-way calls, which may not always be possible due to the PTWA limited availability, would be to obtain local agreements to attend Jobcentres at set times so that information on multiple Participants can be obtained in one visit, which may be a timesaving for both parties. These local visits may also be useful for promoting Confident Futures.

Note: Where the Participant is no longer claiming Universal Credit, you are not required to submit the UCCF02 notification form you should follow your own internal processes. Should you require any support in deciding on the right course of action, contact your Performance Manager.

Safeguarding

Participants with a disability

3.100 Claimants may be referred to the Provision with a disability or disabilities as defined by the Equality Act 2010 or develop them during their time on the Provision.

3.101 The provider shall ensure they deliver support in line with the Equality Act 2010 to enable the Participant to access the Provision equally.

Vulnerable Participants

3.102 Vulnerable Claimants may be referred to the Provision or may be deemed vulnerable during their time on Provision.

3.103 A vulnerable Participant is a Participant who is at greater than normal risk of abuse or neglect. When supporting vulnerable Participants, it is key to make sure they are supported in getting access to the help they need and anyone at risk is protected.

3.104 This should be considered during every interaction with your Participant, both to inform the most appropriate way to engage with your Participant and to identify possible concerns. Your organisation’s policies should support you in making these considerations.

3.105 During engagement with your Participant, you may identify their behaviour or communication as being unusual, for example they may appear frustrated or angry, or may provide brief or one-word answers. Other indicators may help you in identifying and supporting your Participants, in addition to discussions with them and information from Jobcentre Plus. For example non-physical signs such as extreme weight loss and paranoia may indicate addiction, attending appointments with family or friends may indicate learning difficulties.

3.106 You should also consider the involvement of your Participant’s appointee or representative, where they have one, as they may provide additional information to help you provide the most appropriate type of support. Refer to Chapter 3: Supporting Participants on Confident Futures Appointee section.

3.107 All Participants should be aware of support they can access whilst taking part in Confident Futures. This support may include local initiatives and organisations identifiable via your organisation’s local engagement activity and agreed sharing of information methodology. You must signpost your Participants appropriately should they require access to any suitable and available support.

Note: It is important that you maintain professional boundaries when supporting Participants and signposting them to appropriate support. DWP does not require you to make formal referrals to this support as part of Confident Futures.

Note: Where you choose to share your Participants’ information with other organisations you must only do so in line with UK GDPR requirements.

3.108 As a Confident Futures provider, you are permitted to undertake home visits to Participants. However, these should only happen in exceptional circumstances where a safeguarding concern exists. Ensure you consider and implement your own ‘keeping safe’ policy during any home visit.

3.109 You must have safeguarding measures in place to protect the health and well-being of Participants during their time on provision, and to make sure they are supported in getting access to the help they need. You are required to engage with your Participants using a variety of methods which are reflective of their individual circumstances. This must also take into account any known or potential vulnerabilities where you or a PTWA have safeguarding concerns.

3.110 DWP does not prescribe the safeguarding measures which you should include in your approach. However, to support the DWPs safeguarding approach, you should incorporate the following elements within your approach:

prevention - the Participant shall remain at the heart of the approach. You should identify problems which may cause safeguarding concerns, including actions undertaken by you (DA). The adviser should take actions to address this as quickly as possible before harm occurs

review and continuous improvement - you should frequently review and update your safeguarding policy in response to customer experience and emerging safeguarding concerns

awareness of available support - Participants who may be or become a safeguarding concern must be aware of the support available and able to access it during their time on Provision. You should ensure all staff members are familiar with the safeguarding policy and are aware of how they can access available support where appropriate. Participants shall be encouraged to make their own decisions and access support without intrusion

Working with a Participant’s appointee or representative

3.111 A Participant may have an appointee or a representative. It is important to establish whether the person is an appointee or a representative as this will establish how to include this person in your interaction with the Participant. If the Claimant has an appointee at the referral stage, they are eligible to start Confident Futures.

3.112 You will be notified by the PTWA during the referral process where your Participant has a representative. A referral can be made if they have an appointee at referral stage. Similarly, you will be notified by the PTWA via the UCCF01 change of circumstances form where your Participant authorises an appointee or nominates a representative during their time on Confident Futures.

3.113 Where your Participant has an appointee, you should include them in all your discussions as they are responsible for acting on your Participant’s behalf in all dealings with the DWP whilst on Confident Futures. This includes their engagement and participation with you. They will be key to gaining information about your Participant’s circumstances and agreeing appropriate activities during their time on Confident Futures. Appointees are legally empowered to act on behalf of your Participant and there is no need to secure permission to disclose information to them.

3.114 You may wish to engage with your Participant’s representative, where they have one, for example during the first few interactions during their time on Confident Futures or inviting them to attend your interviews. Representatives do not have the same status as appointees but can be valuable in helping your Participant and yourselves during engagement. You must ensure you have your Participant’s explicit consent before disclosing information with their representative.

Participants where English is not their first language or where there are additional communication needs

3.115 You must ensure that you remain compliant with current and future changes in the law as reflected in DWP policy, supporting the Secretary of State in meeting all obligations under the relevant legislation as set out in Confident Futures Terms and Conditions. This includes (but is not limited to):

ensuring Confident Futures supports DWP’s Public Sector Equality Duty as contained in the Equality Act 2010

providing appropriate services to ensure compatibility with the Equality Act 2010 and Welsh Language Act 1993, for example to enable communication with Participants who do not speak English as a first language, or who are deaf, hearing impaired or have a speech impediment

where the provider is operating in an area with a high minority ethnic population, materials in the appropriate minority ethnic language must be made available on request

the requirements set out in the UK GDPR.

3.116 The PTWA will consider, whether Claimants have a communication need (English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL), deaf, visually impaired, hearing impaired or have a speech impediment). Before making a referral, the PTWA will consider all the options of support, including whether other support is better suited to address the Claimant’s needs.

3.117 For Claimants, where English is not their first language or they have communication needs, such as hearing impaired, visually impaired it is the PTWA’s responsibility to ensure access to Confident Futures during the Warm Handover appointment. Following the Warm Handover, for all Participants where English is not their first language or they have communication needs, you will be responsible for ensuring these Participants can access all the services offered through Confident Futures.

3.118 Once a Claimant is referred to Confident Futures, you are required to deliver support in response to these needs throughout the Participant’s time on provision and, where necessary, adapt your approach to ensure clear appropriate support is in place.

Chapter 3d: Travel and travel costs

Travel

3.119 When your Participant agrees to attend a face to face meeting with you, the location must be within 90 minutes of travel from the Participant’s home address to your premises or outreach location. Where a Participant’s health condition limits their ability to travel, you are expected to make appropriate arrangements to meet the Participant, for example at outreach locations.

Travel costs

3.120 You are required to actively promote the access to funding for travel, childcare and other expenses to your Participants throughout their time on Confident Futures and ensure that they are no worse off.

3.121 You must ensure that you comply with current HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) Guidance if you make payments or provide benefits, such as travel cards, to your Participants after they have started work, which relate to that employment. You should inform your Participant that Tax and National Insurance Contributions (NICs) are payable and how this will be done. Failure to account for Tax and NICs that are due on payments made to Participants in employment may be subject to penalties in accordance with current HMRC regulations.

3.122 You must make your Participant aware of any out-of-pocket expenses which they can claim from you for their Initial Meeting, if they attend this face to face, and that they are offered access to, and reimbursement of any appropriate expenses at all future interventions whilst they remain on Confident Futures. You should advise your Participants of the evidence you will need them to produce to claim refunds for new clothing when attending interview or travel costs, such as receipts.

3.123 You are responsible for funding the Participant’s travel costs to attend provision. If the Participant attends interventions arranged by you, for example to undertake work related activities, job interviews, interventions or activities, then you will be responsible for funding their travel costs. You will be required to actively promote the access to funding for travel expenses to Participants throughout their time on provision. There is no requirement to provide a Participant with travel expenses once they have moved into work, however, should you wish to offer to fund travel costs, this will be at your discretion, and will not be claimable from DWP and must be funded by you.

3.124 If your Participant commences work, then you are not responsible for travel costs connected with that employment. Should you wish to offer to fund travel costs, this will be at your discretion and needs to comply with any HMRC guidelines and are not claimable from DWP.

3.125 Whilst your Participants are expected to travel by the cheapest method available to them, there will be occasions where some Participants will be unable to travel by the cheapest method, for example due to a disability. In these instances, you will need to refund any additional costs incurred, which you will have agreed with your Participant, considering all viable options prior to their travel. There is no requirement for you to cover Appointees travel expenses.

Childcare costs

3.126 You will be required to actively promote the access to funding for childcare costs to the Participant throughout their time on provision.

3.127 You must provide funding for childcare, to support your Participant in an activity that you have or are approving, where it has been identified as a barrier for your Participant to achieve agreed goals and objectives. Childcare needs to be provided by the following to qualify for funding:

carers registered with Ofsted

a carer accredited under the Childcare Approval Scheme, run on school premises out of school hours or as an out of hours’ club by a Local Authority

schools or establishments exempted from registration under the Children Act 1989 or operated on Crown property

3.128 Where your Participant makes alternative arrangements due to barriers to participation, costs should only be reimbursed where the provision of childcare falls into one of the above categories.

3.129 Prior to the reimbursement of childcare costs, you must check that the child or children satisfy the age requirement, are a dependant of and reside with your Participant. Support for childcare costs can be paid for each child up to and including the 31 August, following that child’s sixteenth birthday.

3.130 If your Participant commences work, then you are not responsible for childcare costs connected with that employment. Should you wish to offer to fund childcare costs, this will be at your discretion and needs to comply with any HMRC guidelines and are not claimable from DWP.

3.131 To ensure that you or DWP do not take on liability for the safety of children, you must not recommend any particular childcare facilities to your Participants. It is always the Participant’s responsibility to decide whom they entrust with the care of their children. In addition, whilst you may have crèche facilities or childcare facilities on your premises that adhere to current legislation, it must be the parent’s choice to use those facilities.

Replacement care

3.132 You are expected to provide funding for replacement care costs (other than other childcare cost), to support your Participant in an activity that you have, or are approving, where it has been identified as a barrier for your Participant to achieve agreed goals and objectives for Participants who:

are aged 18 or over

are eligible and currently on the Confident Futures scheme

have spent a significant proportion of their lives providing unpaid support to relatives, partners or friends who are ill, frail, disabled or have a mental health or a substance misuse problem

3.133 Prior to agreeing the payment for replacement care costs, you may wish to consider other alternatives, such as moving the time or date of the activity or meeting. Where this is not possible, and replacement care costs have been accepted, then carers must be participating in an approved activity or attending an interview, which has been arranged by you or an employer.

3.134 You need to ensure prior to agreement of funding for any costs that the replacement care is provided by a Local Authority Registered Provider, a Local Authority Preferred Provider, or a recognised care organisation within the local area.

3.135 To ensure that you or DWP do not take on liability for the safety of the individual requiring care you must not recommend any providers, organisations or facilities to your Participant. It is always the responsibility of the carer or person being cared for to make any arrangements.

Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks

3.136 Where your Participant undertakes any activity, in agreement with you, that requires a basic check permitted by the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS), you are responsible for funding any associated costs regarding undertaking this check.

3.137 Note DBS helps employers make safer recruitment decisions each year by processing and issuing DBS checks for England, Wales, the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man. DBS also maintains the adults’ and children’s Barred Lists and makes considered decisions as to whether an individual should be included on one or both of these lists and barred from engaging in regulated activity. Employers will retain the responsibility for the higher-level DBS check if employing your Participant.

Chapter 3e: Change of Circumstances while on Confident Futures

3.138 You must ensure that you hold your Participant’s up to date personal information. Your Participant is responsible for notifying Universal Credit via their Universal Credit account, or by contacting their Jobcentre Plus in writing of any change in their circumstances that occur whilst attending Confident Futures. If you become aware of any change of circumstances which would impact on any benefits your Participant may be in receipt of, you must remind them of their obligation to notify Universal Credit of the change(s).

3.139 The PTWA will send a UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form through unencrypted email to your dedicated inbox with details of any relevant changes to your Participants’ circumstances. In the event of a significant IT failure then a clerical change of circumstances notification form will be issued by the PTWA. If the UCCF01 form is requesting to exit from Confident Futures, it must clearly state one of the exit reasons.

3.140 The PTWA will notify you of the following change of circumstances using the UCCF01 form. This list is not exhaustive:

name

address

phone number

email address

entitlement to benefit and / or change of Labour Market Regime

work search and work availability requirements (including Easements, switching off and tailored conditionality)

appointee / Power of Attorney

outcome of a Self-Employment Gateway Interview

change of Jobcentre and / or PTWA

Participant is in prison or leaves prison

Participant death

exiting the programme

3.141 On receipt of a UCCF01 form you must update your records immediately with any changes to your Participant’s personal information.

3.142 Where the PTWA has notified you on a UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form that a Participants claim to Universal Credit has ended you should discuss whether they wish to continue to participate in Confident Futures.

3.143 Where a Participant wishes to remain on Confident Futures after leaving Universal Credit, Jobcentre Plus support will end and there will be no further requirement for PTWA involvement. You will not be required to arrange further meetings with, or provide further updates to, Jobcentre Plus in relation to that Participant.

3.144 Where a Participant no longer wishes to Participate after leaving Universal Credit you should end their time in PRaP using the appropriate end code.

3.145 Where a Participant’s Universal Credit claim ends before they reach the point at which a Six-Month Touchpoint would normally be arranged, the Six-Month Touchpoint process set out in the Specification and this guidance will not apply, and there will be no requirement to send the UCCF02 notification form to Jobcentre Plus.

3.146 At the point that a Six-Month Touchpoint would normally be carried out, you may undertake a structured review of the Participant’s progress, ongoing support needs and future goals and record the outcome within the Support Plan, including confirming that the Participant wishes to continue receiving support on Confident Futures up to day 365. All other Confident Futures delivery, record-keeping, performance management and contractual reporting requirements remain unchanged.

3.147 If a Participant moves to another Contract Package Area (CPA) within England or Wales, they will remain the responsibility of the original provider. It will be the responsibility of the original provider to arrange appropriate support via their strategic partners to deliver the service requirement until the end of the Participant’s Confident Futures provision.

3.148 For Participants who move outside of England and Wales for a period that is expected to be longer than 90 calendar days, or for a period that is expected to be longer than their remaining time on Confident Futures their time on provision will end. Any Claimants who move to England or Wales from Scotland or Northern Ireland will be considered for any relevant provision, including Confident Futures, using the agreed Job Centre Plus referral routes.

Participant leaves Universal Credit

3.149 A Participant’s circumstances may change during their time on the Confident Future Programme which ends their Universal Credit claim, or they may choose to close their claim. For the avoidance of doubt, a Participant who started Confident Futures while meeting the eligibility criteria may remain on the programme after their Universal Credit claim ends, provided they continue to meet all other participation requirements and choose to remain on the programme.

3.150 DWP will notify you of a change of circumstances including any information regarding participation requirements to inform your ongoing support as appropriate.

3.151 Where you have received official notification of this change via a UCCF01 change of circumstances form, you must continue to offer a service where the Participant has requested to remain on the programme. To provide a clear audit trail, you must ensure that you record evidence of the actions you have taken to facilitate your Participant’s access to your support offer as set out in your contract.

3.152 Should you not receive official notification of this change, you should continue to provide service until you receive a UCCF01 form. You may wish to contact the PTWA, via your local Jobcentre SPoC to confirm the change and request a UCCF01 form as confirmation of this. On receipt of this confirmation, you should follow the actions outlined.

Chapter 3f: Disengagement and re-engagement on Confident Futures

3.154 The disengagement process differs depending on whether the Participant disengages before or after day 182 of provision. Providers should refer to the relevant subsection below before taking action.

3.155 If the Participant Disengages after day 182, you shall close the Participant’s record in PRaP at the end of 10 working days of non-contact. The Participant’s time on Provision shall end at that point. If the Participant Disengages after day 182, you shall close the Participant’s record in PRaP at the end of 10 working day non-contact period and the Participant’s time on Provision shall end at that point. Refer to PRaP End Codes.

3.156 Once a Participant has started on Provision, they will be deemed to have disengaged if they fail to attend an arranged contact and cannot be contacted or re-engaged within 20 working days up to 182 calendar days on programme or 10 working days of non-contact after day 182.

3.157 If the 20 working day non-contact period falls over day 182, you shall close the Participant’s record in PRaP at the end of the 20 working day non-contact period. Re-referrals to Confident Futures will not be permitted. Once the PRaP record is closed, the Participant’s access to support ends permanently in most circumstances. Refer to Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures.

Disengagement process within the first 182 calendar days

3.158 If the Participant fails to attend an arranged contact, you must try to re-engage with them and record details of steps taken to re-engage on the Participant’s Support Plan. You shall contact the Participant within 24 hours of the failure to attend or participate to establish the circumstances of the disengagement, using the method(s) of contact agreed with the Participant.

3.159 Where you are unable to make contact with the Participant, day 1 of the 20-working day non-contact period is activated and you shall attempt to contact the Participant daily, at different times of day, over 5 working days, taking into account what is reasonable and, proportionate to the Participant’s circumstances as set out in their Support Plan.

3.160 You shall then attempt to make contact with the Participant once every 5 working days for the next 15 working days. You shall record on the Participant’s Support Plan the method(s) of communication used to contact the Participant, the date(s) and time(s) of attempted contact.

3.161 If contact is re-established you shall discuss with the Participant the reasons for the non-contact, and if appropriate, options for a break in support, as well as the Participant’s suitability to continue on Provision. The discussion and its outcome should be updated in the Support Plan.

3.162 If the non-contact begins in the first 182 days on provision, the provider shall notify the PTWA on the 21st working day of non-contact.

3.163 Where a Participant disengages at the point of their Six-Month Touchpoint meeting, see Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures Six-Month Touchpoint section.

3.164 Where a Participant remains on Confident Futures after leaving Universal Credit, Jobcentre Plus support will end and there will be no further requirement for PTWA involvement. You will be required to undertake the actions detailed above to attempt to re-engage the Participant however you won’t be required to notify the PTWA on day 21.

Disengagement process after 182 calendar days

3.165 If the non-contact period begins after day 182, you shall notify the PTWA on the 10th working day of non-contact.

3.166 If the non-contact begins after the first 182 calendar days on Provision, you should take the following action:

from day one of non-contact, attempt to contact the Participant daily, at different times of day, over 5 working days, taking into account what is reasonable and proportionate to the Participant’s circumstances as set out in their Support Plan

record on the Participant’s Support Plan the method(s) of communication used to contact the Participant, the date(s) and time(s) of attempted contact

attempt to contact the Participant on the 10th working day, after the first working day of non-contact, taking into account what is reasonable and proportionate to the Participant’s circumstances as set out in their Support Plan

you shall close the Participant’s record in PRaP at the end of the 10th working day non-contact period and the Participant’s time on Provision shall end at that point. Refer to PRaP End Codes

3.167 If you have notified the PTWA of non-contact, you shall notify the PTWA of the re-establishment of contact.

3.168 If contact is re-established during the 5 working day period, you must take the following action:

discuss with the Participant the reasons for the non-contact and, if appropriate, options for a Break, as well as the Participant’s suitability to continue on Provision

update the Support Plan with the discussion and its outcome

3.169 As the Participant’s record will still be open on PRaP, there shall be no digital requirement to formalise the re-establishment of contact.

3.170 Where a Participant remains on Confident Futures after leaving Universal Credit, Jobcentre Plus support will end and there will be no further requirement for PTWA involvement. You will be required to undertake the actions detailed above to attempt to re-engage the Participant however you won’t be required to notify the PTWA.

Provider notifies the PTWA of a Change of Circumstance

3.171 There is no requirement for you to notify DWP of a break (or breaks) in support lasting up to 90 calendar days; with the exception of when a Participant is on a break at the Six-Month Touchpoint, you shall notify the PTWA via UCCF02 notification form and arrange the touchpoint for a date within 20 working days of the end of the break.

3.172 There may be occasions where you need to notify PTWA of disengagement before day 10 of non-contact, including (but not limited to) circumstances involving safeguarding concerns or, risk to vulnerable individuals. In such cases, the provider shall notify the PTWA with immediate effect using the UCCF02 notification form which sets the form priority level to urgent. Further information will be held in the safeguarding section within this document.

Provider notifies DWP of disengagement or re-engagement

3.173 You must notify DWP via UCCF02 notification form when a Participant has disengaged with you or when a Participant has re-engaged with you following a period of disengagement, taking the following action:

notify Jobcentre Plus when the Participant disengages with you, using the UCCF02 notification form sent via unencrypted email. You shall include, in Part 5 of the form, the date the form is emailed to the Jobcentre

notify Jobcentre Plus when the Participant re-engages using the UCCF02 notification form sent by unencrypted email

PTWA contact following Participant disengagement (first 182 calendar days only)

3.174 The process described in this section applies only where a Participant disengages within the first 182 calendar days of their participation on Confident Futures. Where the 20 working day non-contact period falls over day 182, you shall close the Participant’s PRaP record at the end of the 20 working day non-contact period. Where a Participant disengages after day 182, the provider must follow the disengagement process and close the Participant’s PRaP record at the end of the 10 working day non-contact period.

3.175 The PTWA will contact the Participant after receiving the UCCF02 notification form notifying them of a voluntary Participant disengagement from the programme. They will try to find out why the Participant has disengaged and encourage them to re-engage. The PTWA will contact Participant once via their journal message and allow 7 calendar days for the Participant to respond to them.

3.176 The PTWA will notify you of the outcome using a UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form within 15 working days of receipt of the UCCF02 notification form via the designated Jobcentre inbox, using the date recorded in Part 5 of the UCCF02 form.

3.177 Where the Participant responds and confirms that they wish to re-engage, the PTWA will record this outcome on the UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form and signpost the Participant back to you.

3.178 Where the Participant does not respond to the journal message within 7 calendar days, or the PTWA is otherwise unable to establish contact with them, the PTWA will record this outcome on the UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form. The Participant will remain on programme until day 182. Once day 182 has elapsed, you may claim an end line in PRaP.

3.179 Where a Participant has been contacted and wishes to have a break from the programme, a PTWA will notify you of the outcome on a UCCF01 change of circumstances form and signpost the Participant back to you. On receipt of change of circumstances form UCCF01, you shall contact the Participant to discuss their request for a break, update the Support Plan with duration of break, any agreed keeping in touch arrangements and a date to resume participation.

3.180 Where a Participant has been contacted and wishes to end their participation on the programme, a PTWA will notify you of the outcome through a UCCF01 change of circumstances form, on receipt of the form you can claim an end line in PRaP.

Actions for provider

on receipt of the UCCF01 form, update the Participants record with the outcome as notified to you. Where you have been notified that a Participant will be re-engaging with you arrange to contact them and continue to support them for the remainder of their time on the Programme

notify Jobcentre Plus when the Participant re-engages using the UCCF02 notification form sent via unencrypted email

where you have been notified that a Participant will not be re-engaging with you update Participant’s Support Plan with the reason for disengagement as notified to you and can claim an end line in PRaP

where Jobcentre Plus is unable to confirm the Participants status you will receive a notification via UCCF01 change of circumstances form. Participant will remain on the programme until day 182. When day 182 has lapsed, you can claim an end line in PRaP

Chapter 3g: Breaks in support on Confident Futures

3.182 To mitigate risk of disengagement or early exit from support, you should offer Participants a break in support when required, for example where circumstances affect the Participant’s ability to engage with planned support (such as following a medical procedure and recovery. The Dedicated Adviser should inform Participants of the option for breaks during their Initial Meeting. Any break must be agreed between the Participant, and their Dedicated Adviser. Breaks should not exceed a cumulative total of 90 calendar days across the 365-day support period.

3.183 Providers should discuss the circumstances and how long the Participant expects them to last. If in exceptional circumstances the break (or breaks) is expected to last more than 90 calendar days, the provider should discuss with the Participant whether the support is still appropriate for them and consider other options with them, such as returning to PTWA support. Where the Participant opts to return to Jobcentre Plus support, they will be considered an early completer/completer. See Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures for further details on next steps. The Participant may decide to remain on provision in this case record their reasons in the Support Plan, update it accordingly, and continue providing appropriate support.

3.184 There is no requirement for the provider to notify DWP of a break (or breaks) in support lasting up to 90 days, with the exception of when you are aware that the break will fall over the dates that the Partcipants’ Six-Month Touchpoint should be held. In these circumstances, notify the PTWA using form UCCF02 of the break and the date it is anticipated to end. Details of any breaks taken between zero and 182 days, and any related discussions, should be reviewed at the Six-Month Touchpoint.

Note: You are not required to notify the PTWA of the break where the Participant is not in receipt of Universal Credit.

3.185 The support period will continue to run during any breaks in participation, and the total duration of support will not be extended beyond the maximum 365-day entitlement.

3.186 All breaks in support and discussions concerning them must be recorded in the Support Plan.

Chapter 3h: In-Work Support (IWS) on Confident Futures

3.187 IWS will be provided to Participants who move into employment. For those Participants entering work, and with their consent, you should, complete an Employment Support Plan (ESP) and issue it to the employer within 10 working days of the Participant entering Employment or self-employment.

3.188 IWS will be in place for either the remainder of the Participants time on the programme (up to 365 days from their start date) or until the they no longer require it.

3.189 In the rare event where a Participant does not agree to an ESP being produced, you must ensure this decision is clearly documented, dated, and formally recorded in their Support Plan. Supporting evidence should also be retained to support compliance and assurance activities. If the Participant wants to remain on the programme you should continue to provide tailored IWS to them and continue to update their Support Plan.

3.190 If a Participant moves into employment, remind the Participant to notify their PTWA as per Chapter 3e: Change of Circumstances while on Confident Futures. They may decide they do not require IWS, and they can choose to end their participation in the programme at this point. Refer to Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures and Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures for action to take for completers in this scenario.

Note: You should not request the Participant to notify the PTWA if they are not in receipt of Universal Credit.

3.191 You will be responsible for the design of the ESP which must set out the support you will give to the Participant and the employer during the IWS period, for the duration of the programme (up to 365 calendar days), to help the Participant sustain employment. It will also include the Participant’s support needs from the employer after you are no longer involved, after the period of IWS. The ESP should contain as a minimum:

a description of the IWS you are providing to the Participant

any actions required of the Participant in relation to the IWS

all Non-Confident Futures Activities

3.192 You must provide tailored IWS to both the Participant and the employer to help the Participant stay in work, except where the Participant has stated they do not require it. The IWS should be provided by the same Dedicated Adviser, and to the same frequency and intensity as during the pre-employment support phase.

3.193 The same level of support will be expected for those Participants who choose to become self-employed. It is not intended that you would act in a small business advisor capacity, rather you should continue to support the Participant with on-going management of their barriers to work as you would with an employed Participant. You should signpost the Participant towards agencies that can support them with appropriate business advice, including helping the Participant to access the Access to Work (AtW) provision.

3.194 Support for each Participant must include, but is not limited to:

maintaining frequency of contact (at least once every 4 calendar weeks) with Participant, with any additional contact as required

where appropriate, the Participant being accompanied to the workplace by the Dedicated Adviser, and the Dedicated Adviser supporting the Participant in meetings with the Participant’s line manager and colleagues

on-going engagement with the Participant’s wider sustainable support network (both formal and informal networks)

practical actions, for example socialising and integration in the work environment, journey planning, pre-start visits for familiarisation, establishing a buddy in the workplace

facilitating any reasonable adjustments required and where appropriate, ensuring Access to Work (AtW) assistance is in place from the from the start of employment

3.195 The ESP must be updated when the Participant enters employment or self-employment and at least every 4 calendar weeks throughout IWS. Where Participant has stated they do not want an ESP, you should update the Support Plan.

3.196 Check the possible impact on the Participant’s welfare benefits of any paid employment undertaken and ensure these are understood by the Participant.

Confident Futures employer support offer

3.197 You will be expected to have and to build strong links to national and local employers, helping to build disability confidence and to increase the capacity and sustainability of employers including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to recruit and retain disabled people.

3.198 You must provide a full employer support offer focussed on working with the employer so that the employer can continue to support the Participant in work after the provision has ended. The employer support offer will include meeting with employers and their staff and encouraging employers to find champions/advocates within their workplace. This will also involve up-skilling employers and developing a support network that will continue to work together to meet the Participant’s needs and help them to sustain employment.

3.199 You have a role in developing the confidence of the employers you work with in the delivery of the Provision to accommodate disabled people in their workplace and to understand the principles of “Disability Confident”. This includes increasing an employer’s disability awareness and capability. You will need to ensure that employers are able to continue to support each Participant with their support network and AtW where appropriate once the delivery of IWS on Confident Futures ends.

Local tailoring and stakeholder engagement

take the lead in establishing and facilitating regular partnership engagement meetings where partnership forums do not exist within a CPA

As such, you must develop and maintain effective working relationships with relevant local health partners to ensure coordinated support for Participants’ health-related barriers.

other relevant stakeholders as required

Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures

4.1 This chapter sets out the steps that you and PTWA will take to ensure that all Confident Futures Participants complete at the appropriate stage in their journey. The Customer Service Standard covered in this chapter is Customer Service Standard 3.

4.2 A Participant will become an Early Completer when they finish on provision before the Six-Month Touchpoint (between the day they start on the programme (day 1) and up to and including day 182 of their participation).

4.3 A Participant will become a Completer when they finish on provision between day 183 and day 365.

4.4 Where a Participant decides to end their time on the Provision and return to Jobcentre Plus support at any point during their time on Provision or reaches 365 days on Provision, you shall lead a 40-minute formal Warm Handback with the Participant and the PTWA. The meeting shall be conducted via the Participant’s preferred channel of engagement (for example, face to face, phone call, or video call), with the Authority’s preference being face to face delivery at a local Jobcentre Plus (subject to local arrangements). Any reasonable accessibility requirements shall be accommodated. You shall complete a UCCF02 Notification form to request the scheduling of the Warm Handback.

Note: If the Participant is no longer in receipt of Universal Credit there is no requirement to have a Warm Handback.

4.5 Where the Participant will complete 365 calendar days of support, you shall start to plan for the Warm Handback 20 working days in advance of the Participant’s formal end date on Provision. At any other time, you shall start to plan within one working day of the Participant confirming their wish to return to Jobcentre Plus support.

4.6 You shall ensure that the Participant’s Support Plan is in place and up-to-date and that a Progress Report is completed and added to this.

Warm Handback

4.7 The Warm Handback shall be informed by the Support Plan and Progress Report, enabling a shared understanding of the Participant’s progress and achievements during their time on Provision, their current circumstances and their ongoing needs. The Warm Handback shall provide the Participant with a clear understanding of their next steps and the ongoing support they will receive from the Jobcentre Plus. Following completion of the Warm Handback, you shall formally ‘end’ the Participant on PRaP within 2 working days by claiming the end line in PRaP.

4.8 A Warm Handback will not be required in cases where the Participant transitions to employment or support that is not delivered via Jobcentre Plus (for example an alternative employment support programme). A Participant may choose to complete their time on Confident Futures provision, or, in certain circumstances, their time on provision will end.

4.9 Participants’ time on programme will end in the following circumstances:

when the Participant moves outside of England or Wales for a period longer than 90 calendar days, or a period that is expected to be longer than the Participant’s remaining time on Confident Futures; or

has a custodial sentence and is residing at His Majesty’s prison for a period longer than 90 calendar days; or

no longer has the right to work or reside in the UK; or

Participant death; or

moves into full-time education or training; or

moves into alternative DWP-funded provision

4.10 Where the Participant chooses to end their participation on the programme, you should attempt to address any new circumstances/ needs before discussing early completion/completion with the Participant. If both parties agree that early completion/completion is the best option, you should notify the PTWA via a UCCF02 notification form and, where the Participant has indicated a wish to return to Jobcentre Plus support, arrange a Warm Handback.

4.11 The ultimate decision as to whether to leave or remain on provision will be made by the Participant, other than when the circumstances at paragraph 4.21 apply.

4.12 If a Participant becomes ineligible during their time on the Provision, you shall:

ensure the Participant has the choice to remain on the Provision unless their change of circumstances makes them ineligible (see paragraph 4.21)

discuss the available options with the Participant, who should consider their own suitability to continue on Confident Futures

4.13 If these changes happen before day 182, the Six-Month Touchpoint will give the Participant the opportunity to discuss whether they wish to remain on the provision for a further 6 months. Refer to Chapter 3: Supporting Participants on Confident Futures for more information about the Six- Month Touchpoint.

Confident Futures Completer Progress Report

4.14 You shall complete a Progress Report for each Participant to inform the Six-Month Touchpoint and the Warm Handback. These may coincide where a Participant exits the Provision at the Six-Month Touchpoint.

4.15 You shall ensure that the Progress Report shall:

summarise progress against the Support Plan aims and objectives, including actions completed and any experience gained in a working environment

reflect any changes in the Participant’s support needs during their time on Provision

identify current barriers to progress

clearly set out the agreed next steps

4.16 You shall prepare the Progress Report during the final meeting between the Participant and the Dedicated Adviser before the Six-Month Touchpoint and the Warm Handback. You shall use the Progress Report to inform discussions at these meetings. You shall finalise the Progress Report during the Six-month touchpoint discussion and include the Participant’s decision on whether they wish to continue on or exit support and the reasons for this.

4.17 The Progress Report shall be included in the Support Plan as an addendum and, if the Participant continues on support after the Six-Month Touchpoint, it shall be updated and finalised at the Warm Handback when the Participant exits Provision.
