Chapter 6: Health and safety, accidents, unacceptable behaviour, fraud prevention and complaints

6.1 This chapter pulls together various key pieces of information that you will need to be aware of in respect of working with your Participants and also details what you must have in place to ensure Participants who are unhappy with the service they receive are able to raise a confidential complaint, and the processes you must follow to respond and resolve any issues raised.

Health and safety

6.2 All Participants on Confident Futures are entitled to train and work in a healthy and safe environment with due regard to their welfare. Under Health and Safety Law they are regarded as your employees, whether they are paid by you or not. You must, therefore, comply with your Duty of Care under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and the Act’s associated regulations in the same way as you would do for any other member of your workforce.

6.3 You must ensure that your Participants receive appropriate health and safety induction, training and supervision, and that systems are in place for checking this, both within your own organisation and at any of your supply chain partners.

6.4 You must complete risk assessments, instruct, inform and train your Participants on the control measures identified. There are specific risk assessments for young people, pregnant workers, lone workers and employees who are engaged in manual handling activities. In addition, there may be specific risks flagged by the PTWA such as Participants who have restrictions imposed on them by probation for example, they are not allowed to use IT due to probation conditions in the short or long term etc.

6.5 DWP may visit you and your supply chain partners for a variety of reasons. When doing so, we will, in the course of our duties, adopt an ‘awareness’ approach to health and safety. In doing this we will not be conducting a health and safety inspection, nor will we be able to offer advice on whether something is safe or not. Instead, we will approach this from the position of any layperson.

6.6 However, if we do spot something on which we require assurance or clarification we will raise this with you or your supply chain partner’s representative at the location we are visiting. If it is subsequently decided that the issue raised is one that requires follow up action, this will be arranged with you through your Performance Manager (PM).

Accidents

Arrangements for managing and reporting accidents

6.7 In reporting and managing accidents, which involve a Confident Futures Participant, you and your supply chain partners may wish to consider using similar or the same procedures as you use for existing employees. However, these procedures should ensure that:

immediate action is taken to ensure the safety of your Participants and prevent reoccurrence

all accidents, including minor incidents, are recorded in your accident book

all accidents covered by the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations 2013 (RIDDOR) are reported to the appropriate enforcing authority

an investigation is carried out to assess whether any changes should be made to the workplace or procedures following the accident or incident

Risk Assessment Control Measures are reviewed and, if necessary, revised to ensure their effectiveness and that they remain suitable and sufficient

6.8 In doing this, you will wish to take into account the full range of factors relating to the incident including, for example, whether:

your Participant had received appropriate Health and Safety awareness and instruction and that they understood the implications

the activities undertaken by your Participant at the time of the accident were required as part of Confident Futures

supervision was adequate

appropriate clothing and equipment were being used

the work environment was organised in a safe manner

6.9 Should your Participant need to make a claim to an industrial injuries benefit you should direct them to the Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit (IIDB) site on gov.uk for an application form and contact details for the IIDB contact Centre.

Unacceptable behaviour

6.10 Participants on Confident Futures have a responsibility to behave in an appropriate manner just as they would if they were in employment. You should explain what constitutes appropriate behaviour as part of the induction.

6.11 Where cases of misconduct or unacceptable behaviour by your Participants arise, you should immediately deal with it in the most appropriate manner. Where the inappropriate behaviour is of a minor nature, such as an initial refusal to co-operate, you should aim to handle the issue internally in the first instance. It is important that you keep an audit trail of all misconduct communications and record the situation, date and method of communication used to address this in case this is needed for investigation at a later date.

6.12 If an incident is more serious or there is a pattern of unacceptable behaviour, for example, damage to property or continued refusal to co-operate with reasonable requests, you should notify the PTWA or other nominated contact point.

6.13 You are required to notify the PTWA of all incidents of unacceptable behaviour that involve your Participants. We consider the following as examples of unacceptable behaviour:

violence

verbal abuse, including that of a sexual or racist nature

threats, which are implied or otherwise;

intimidation

sexual innuendo

harassment

unwelcome attention

attempted or actual assaults

inappropriate use of the internet or provider’s IT system

This list is not exhaustive.

6.14 When notifying DWP of an incident you should complete the UCCF02 form and select urgent 2-way call and send to the appropriate designated Jobcentre Inbox. You should then contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC and advise that you have submitted the form and require an urgent call.

Exclusions from provider premises

6.15 Only in extreme circumstances should you request that your Participant be excluded from your site(s). Before any such request, you are required to attempt to manage your Participant within your business, moving them to an alternative site where available and necessary. As a last resort you may request that your Participant is excluded from your site(s).

Note: This is not exclusion from Confident Futures, only from your site(s).

6.16 If your Participant’s behaviour is consistently unacceptable and other methods of engaging or issuing verbal or written warnings prove ineffectual, you may wish to request that your Participant is excluded from your premises. The situation must be one of genuine risk to staff and not just because your Participant is difficult, and you must supply evidence about why exclusion is appropriate.

6.17 If exclusion is sought, a request should be made via your Performance Manager who will forward the details to the PTWA for a decision to be made based on the individual circumstances.

6.18 Participants will not be excluded based on potentially violent or inappropriate behaviour (for example, racial or sexual verbal assault, foul language or the issuing of threats, or if your Participant refuses to engage). However, you must show a duty of care to your Participants and staff and in certain circumstances the only immediate option may be to temporarily remove your Participant from the situation.

6.19 In some circumstances your Participants who have a Keep Customer Interactions Safe (KCIS) safety measure marker recorded against them may be considered as posing a risk to the health and safety of staff. These Participants will be subjected to certain control measures to ensure staff safety. Further information on your Participant’s KCIS safety measure marker can be requested by contacting the Jobcentre Plus SPoC.

6.20 Examples of behaviours that would result in control measures being implemented would be where a Participant:

has committed an actual physical assault on a member of staff or another Participant, regardless of injury

has committed an actual physical assault on a member of staff’s family

has attempted to commit a physical assault on a member of staff or another Participant

stalked a member of staff or another Participant (which is defined as “the wilful, malicious and repeated following and harassing of another person”)

suffers from a severe mental illness, and a qualified medical practitioner or social worker states that they are likely to pose a danger to staff

has made a threat of violence either face to face, over the phone, or in writing

has displayed threatening or aggressive behaviour

6.21 Where incidents such as this occur or where control measures have been introduced by Jobcentre Plus then you may decide how best you can handle your Participant, suggested controls include:

holding interviews in public areas

having a colleague present at interviews

informing senior staff or managers of interview details

Fast Track Incidents

6.22 While all incidents of unacceptable Participant behaviour are serious, some may have to be afforded a particular importance and dealt with as a priority because of their nature and circumstances.

6.23 When notifying DWP of an incident you should complete the UCCF02 form and select urgent 2-way call and send to the appropriate designated Jobcentre Inbox. You should then contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC and advise that you have submitted the form and require an urgent call if an incident occurs that can be defined as a ‘serious’ or ‘fast track’ incident.

Note: Where the Participant is no longer claiming Universal Credit, you are not required to submit the UCCF02 notification form you should follow your own internal processes. Should you require any support in deciding on the right course of action contact your Performance Manager.

6.24 A serious incident is an incident which compromises the health and safety of DWP staff or the staff of our supply chain partners, or our ability to safely use our premises. The serious nature or sensitivity of the incident warrants an immediate notification to senior management, prior to further investigation.

Note: This also applies when the Participant is on work experience or periods of attachment to an employer, in addition to time spent with yourself or supply chain partners.

6.25 Sometimes a serious incident may not neatly fit within the criteria below (this list is not exhaustive):

actual assault (intentional physical contact) has occurred - which is directed at DWP or partner employees in connection with their duties

weapon, or other item presenting a similar level of threat, has been used to harm, attempt to harm or intimidate

is significant disruption to normal business

is a significant cost implication (such as, estimated at over £2,000) for your business, DWP or your supply chain partners’ business, for example, damage to property

has been a viable targeted or personalised threat (and police advice has been sought)

suicide, attempted suicide or self-harm incident, understood to be directly connected to DWP business

6.26 Incidents occurring on either your own, your supply chain, co-located premises, or in your Participants home may need to be Fast Tracked. If this is the case, you should submit the UCCF02 notification form and alert your Jobcentre Plus SPoC immediately via telephone, who will raise the incident on your behalf. You should also make your Performance Manager aware, as soon as possible. If you are unclear as to whether an incident should be considered a Fast Track, you should contact your Performance Manager for further advice and support.

Overview of Incident Referral Process

6.27 Outlined below is the process you should follow to manage Participant behaviour following an incident.

1. Report the incident

complete the UCCF02 form and select urgent 2-way call and send to the appropriate designated Jobcentre In box

you should then contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC and advise that you have submitted the form and require an urgent call

2. Attempt to manage the Participant’s behaviour

take appropriate steps to address and manage the behaviour

3. Determine whether the incident has been resolved

if yes, no further action is required

if no, continue to Step 4

4. Consider whether the Participant has consistently ignored attempts to resolve the issue

if no, continue to manage the Participant’s behaviour and make further attempts to resolve the issue

if yes, continue to Step 5

5. Implement appropriate control measures

Put suitable control measures in place to help resolve the issue.

6. Review the effectiveness of the control measures

if the control measures have resolved the issue, no further action is required

if the control measures have not resolved the issue, continue to Step 7

7. Request a Joint Review

contact your local Jobcentre Plus office via a UCCF02 and request an urgent two-way conversation. Follow this with a call to your Jobcentre Plus SPoC to advise you have submitted the form to request the call

during the review, consider whether exclusion from your premises is appropriate and can be agreed

Complaints Overview

6.28 A complaint is defined by DWP as any expression of dissatisfaction about the service provided which is not resolved by operational staff as normal business.

6.29 There should be no barriers to your Participants making a complaint – they or the person, organisation or professional body representing them should be able to make a complaint in the manner which best suits their communication needs.

6.30 You shall explain the feedback and complaints processes to the Participant when they start Confident Futures Services as part of their induction.

6.31 Information about your complaint process should be widely available and easily understood by your staff and Participants. It should include details of the complaint process, timescales for responding and details of how to escalate a complaint if your Participant is not satisfied with your final response to their complaint.

6.32 To meet these expectations, you must:

have a complaint process in place for yourself and across the whole of your supply chain which can be easily accessed by your Participants or their representatives

explain your internal complaints process to your Participants during your first contact with them. Refer to Chapter 3

take all steps outlined in your internal procedure to resolve the complaint at the earliest possible opportunity

complete all action to your stated timescales

ensure you retain a full log of complaints received, correspondence and phone calls as well as the complaint outcome in case this is information needed for an Independent Case Examiner (ICE) referral and/or DWP audit teams. DWP may also request and expect you to supply this data on an ad hoc basis

ensure your Participants are aware of their rights to bring their complaint to the ICE within 6 months of your final response.

final responses from you must inform Participants that they can refer their complaint to the ICE if they remain dissatisfied after completing the complaints process

Note: Although ICE will generally not require you to provide evidence of your actions following any recommendations that are made, there may be exceptions where ICE will request this information and providers will be made aware of this when signing off any report recommendations.

Note: Do not advise Participants to contact ICE before getting a final response from you as they will not investigate the complaint. Refer to How to bring a complaint to the Independent Case Examiner.

6.33 After following all steps in your complaints process, you must include in your final response to your Participant a standard text which informs the customer to contact ICE should they wish to pursue their complaint. The text can be found in Annex 6.2.

6.34 Note: A final response can be written or verbal, but in all instances must include the information shown at Annex 6.2.

6.35 It is your responsibility to resolve any dissatisfaction, concerns or complaints internally through your own process. However, in some circumstances it may be necessary to contact the PTWA or your Performance Manager in the first instance for additional advice.

Responding to and handling complaints

6.36 Where your Participant is unhappy with the service they are receiving from you or Jobcentre Plus in relation to delivery of Confident Futures, they may raise a complaint. On occasions you may also receive complaints from employers or enquiries on your Participant’s behalf from elected officials.

6.37 The following section describes the steps you must take in each different scenario to respond to and resolve complaints.

1. Participant makes a complaint against your organisation or staff directly to you:

take all steps outlined in your procedure to resolve the complaint

take all action to your stated timescale

on reaching the end of your process you must include the information at Annex 6.2 in your final response

2. Participant makes a complaint against you to Jobcentre Plus:

Jobcentre Plus staff will direct your Participant to raise their issue with you so you have an opportunity to resolve it to their satisfaction

on receipt of the complaint, you should follow your complaints procedure as normal

you must deal with your Participant’s complaint in the same way you would have done had they raised it with you directly

3. Participant makes a mixed complaint (against you and Jobcentre Plus):

if your Participant raises this type of complaint with you, you should direct them to their PTWA. The Participant can raise their complaint with Jobcentre Plus either face to face in the Jobcentre or via their Universal Credit Account

Jobcentre Plus will lead on responding to your Participant and will ask for a contribution from you regarding the element of the complaint which relates to your service

if you are contacted by Jobcentre Plus, you should where possible, return any evidence or contribution within the stated timescales, or if a deadline has not been stated within a maximum of 5 working days

Jobcentre Plus will issue the final response, inclusive of your contribution, to your Participant

if your Participant remains dissatisfied at this point, they will be advised to approach you directly about any issues which relate to the service you provide

you should treat the first combined response from Jobcentre Plus as the first stage of your complaints process and escalate your Participant’s issue to the next stage of your complaint procedure

Jobcentre Plus will deal independently with any remaining issues relating to its services

4. Participant makes a complaint to you about Confident Futures policy. If a Participant raises a complaint with you regarding participation in Confident Futures or any other issue relating to Confident Futures policy, you should direct them to contact the Jobcentre Plus team dealing with their case to try to resolve the issue.

5. An employer makes a complaint about you regarding the Confident Futures.

During the life of the contract an employer, with whom you have placed or attempted to place a Participant, may wish to raise a complaint about you:

on receipt of the complaint, you should follow your procedure as normal

you must deal with the employer’s complaint in the same way as you would any complaint made against you

6. An elected member of a national or international body makes a complaint to you on behalf of your Participant There may be occasions when an elected member of a national or international body would write to you on behalf of your Participant, for example:

Member of Parliament (MP)

Member of the National Assembly for Wales (AM)

These representatives do have the authority to act on behalf of your Participant, but where you have any doubt about responding to the elected member, you can ask for confirmation that they are acting on behalf of your Participant.

If the elected member came to DWP on behalf of your Participant with feedback that involved both DWP and yourself, DWP will co-ordinate a joint response by getting a contribution from you.

7. Participant wishes to make a complaint about DWP or Jobcentre Plus

The Participant is advised to follow DWP’s complaints procedure .

Independent Case Examiner (ICE) role and processes

6.38 The ICE Office provides an impartial resolution and investigation service for people who are unhappy with the way their complaint has been dealt with.

6.39 ICE have 2 primary objectives:

to act as an independent adjudicator if your Participant considers that they have not been treated fairly or have not had their complaints dealt with in a satisfactory manner

to support service improvements by providing constructive comment and meaningful systemic recommendations

Who can raise a complaint to ICE?

6.40 Participants who are unhappy with the way in which their complaint has been dealt with by either DWP or their contracted service providers.

6.41 To raise a complaint with ICE the Participant must meet the following criteria:

have given you or DWP the opportunity to respond and resolve the issue

have received the final response, that explained that they can take their complaint to ICE if they are not satisfied with the response they have received

raise the complaint with ICE within 6 months of receiving the final response from yourself or DWP

Note: ICE will only accept complaints for investigation if they meet all 3 of these criteria.

What happens when a case is raised with ICE?

6.42 After they accept a complaint, ICE will contact you to confirm that each step of your internal process has been completed. If they feel that you have not completed your process satisfactorily you may be asked to revisit some steps to seek resolution before ICE are prepared to investigate further.

Note: ICE will generally only consider a complaint after your own complaints process has been completed and a final response has been issued. If internal complaint stages have not been exhausted, ICE may not investigate.

6.43 You must deal with any correspondence of any nature from ICE within the stated timescales and at least within 5 working days.

6.44 Once ICE has accepted a case, they will work to resolve the case by taking the following 3 stage approach, attempting to resolve matters at the earliest possible stage. At every stage, you will have the opportunity to give your version of events and offer any supporting evidence.

6.45 See the Complaint resolution core briefing pack: DWP provider guidance and refer to stage 1 Resolution, Stage 2 Settlement and Stage 3 Investigation Report in Chapter 4: ICE.

The Public Service Ombudsman (PSO)

6.46 Participants have no right of appeal against ICE’s decision. However, if your Participant is unhappy with the outcome of the ICE investigation, they can ask their MP to refer their case to the PSO. If the PSO accepts their case and upholds the complaint they may recommend additional remedies including financial redress for your Participant, which you would also be liable to pay. For more information, visit the PSO website.

Fraud prevention

6.47 If you suspect that your Participant is committing fraud you should follow the procedures outlined on Report benefit fraud.

6.48 DWP places the utmost importance on the need to prevent fraud and irregularity in the delivery of its contracts. You are required to, as a minimum, adhere to the following 4 principles:

have an established system that enables your staff to report inappropriate behaviour by colleagues in respect of any claims for payment in relation to Confident Futures contract

ensure that your (and your supply chain partners) performance management systems do not encourage individual staff to make false claims for payment in relation to Confident Futures contract

ensure a segregation of duties within your and your supply chain operations between those staff directly involved in delivering the services and those making claims for payment in relation to the Confident Futures contract

establish an audit system to provide periodic checks, at a minimum 6 monthly intervals, to ensure effective and accurate recording and reporting of performance of the services

6.49 You are reminded that you must endeavour to safeguard funding of the contract against fraud generally and, fraud on the part of your directors, employees or sub-contractors. You must pay the utmost regard to safeguarding public funds against misleading claims for payment and shall notify us immediately, via the DWP Security inbox, if you have reason to suspect that any serious irregularity or internal fraud has occurred or is occurring.

6.50 If you, your staff or your supply chain partners commit fraud in relation to any contract with DWP, we may:

terminate the contract and recover from you the amount of any loss suffered by DWP resulting from the termination, including the cost reasonably incurred by DWP of making other arrangements for the supply of the services and any additional expenditure incurred by DWP throughout the remainder of the contract period, or

recover in full, from you any other loss sustained by DWP

6.51 You are required to report all incidents of allegations of provider fraud to DWP via the email address: securityincident.responseteam-sirt-@dwp.gov.uk and copy the Commercial Restart Team at commercialdirectorate.restartteam@dwp.gov.uk.

Alternatively, you can follow the Fraud Reporting Process on Report benefit fraud.

6.52 You must co-operate fully with DWP and assist in the identification of any of your Participants who may be unlawfully claiming state benefits. We may from time to time brief you as to the co-operation and assistance we require, including the provision of information regarding fraud by your Participants. On receipt of the information, further evidence may be collected by DWP or other department, office or agency of His Majesty’s government with a view to prosecution.

7.36 If you receive a Right of Access request from a Claimant or Participant solicitor or third-party, you must forward immediately to the Right of Access Gateway Team at rightofaccess.requests@dwp.gov.uk.

7.37 The Gateway Team has 30 days in which to respond to the Right of Access request and communicate this to you. This only applies to data where DWP is the data controller, or a joint data controllership exists with DWP. Where you are the independent data controller you should follow your internal procedures.

Right to erase Participant information

7.38 There may be occasions when you receive a request from a Participant to erase their personal information from your records.

7.39 Upon receipt of the request, you should acknowledge the request from the Participant and issue a holding response immediately detailing that the query will be dealt with within one month.

7.40 You should forward the details of the request, including the PRaP PO Number to the following email addresses: data.protectionofficer@dwp.gov.uk.

7.41 You will receive a generic email containing a reference number and the actions that you should take from the Data Protection Office (DPO) team. The reference number must be used with all correspondence with the DPO team.

7.42 You will receive a response back from Confident Futures Live Running Policy Team accepting or rejecting the request for erasure. It is your responsibility to pass this on to the Participant.

Marketing and publicity

7.43 As part of Confident Futures offer you are required to supply engaging marketing materials (in line with DWP guidelines) to ensure that PTWAs and Claimants are clearly informed about your support offer.

7.44 For this chapter, ‘marketing materials’ are any form of branded material used by yourselves to promote Confident Futures. This includes printed (and other format) materials such as:

induction packs

banners

information posters

flyers

brochures

leaflets and

presentations

7.45 Marketing material can also easily be adapted into digital forms and may include items such as social media posts, e-newsletters and blogs.

Planning your marketing and communications activity

7.46 As a contracted provider of DWP we would encourage you to share your own planned marketing activity with Jobcentre Plus locally. This will ensure that both DWP and providers are able to maximise the value of their communications.

7.47 As you are best placed to know the demographics of your local area, it is up to you to decide the best way to promote and describe your services in relation to Confident Futures. This includes deciding what types of products, activities and channels you want to use to market or communicate your services.

7.48 Marketing should be for the purposes of providing information about the offer to PTWA and Claimants. You may also choose to raise external awareness and announce your role in delivering the offer for publicity purposes.

7.49 All the marketing products you produce must adhere to the standards, as written in your contract. These standards are in place to protect the integrity of Confident Futures and the reputation of DWP.

No logos, trademarks, branding, partnership statements, affiliations, endorsements, or other representations relating to another programme, DWP funded or otherwise, may be used in a way that implies or suggests an association with Confident Futures. This applies to all:

programme materials

Participant communications

websites

social media channels

marketing content

venue signage

other promotional activities

The ‘Confident Futures’ name must appear prominently across all public facing materials. The following sets out acceptable Confident Futures naming conventions:

the ‘Confident Futures name cannot be used merely as a page footer; it must be prominent

the ‘Confident Futures’ name can appear alongside Supplier branding, but it shall be prominent

‘Confident Futures’ must be written in full; and use the correct Funded by UK Government’ logo

7.53 Information on how to access the correct Funded by UK Government logo is available on the DWP Basecamp portal. The portal address has already been provided to you by DWP. There is no requirement to register or sign in. Simply download the ZIP file, which contains:

the logo in both black and white (for light backgrounds) and white (for dark backgrounds)

in EPS file format (for use in professional design software)

as a PNG image file with a transparent background

and an SVG image file that can be used on Word or PowerPoint documents

7.54 You shall supply marketing material to Jobcentre Plus outlining the Confident Futures Services you will offer to Participants. The marketing material shall be used to support discussions between the PTWA and Claimant prior to a Referral.

7.55 DWP shall pre-approve marketing and publicity material which shall be shared with Jobcentre Plus to be held on Jobcentre Plus’s IT systems only. This is in addition to the naming conventions set out in paragraph 7.52 above.

7.56 Any material you produce specifically for marketing Confident Futures must clearly show that it is a government programme.

7.57 Some key issues you must consider for the content of your marketing, communications and press activity are:

reputational risk - materials you produce must not adversely affect the reputation of the service being provided by the Government, DWP or Jobcentre Plus, for example risks that could lead to adverse media attention, or messages that could be misunderstood or misinterpreted

7.58 More information about delivering inclusive communications is available from the Office for Disability Issues.

Communication standards

should be relevant to the service you are providing

Good news stories

7.61 As Participants begin to achieve positive outcomes from the support provided, and for some this may include securing employment, providers may wish to utilise marketing materials to communicate the success of Confident Futures. Marketing materials review and approval process

Submitting material for review during programme live running

This document can be found in Confident Futures All Providers file share directory, within the provider guidance folder in Employment Programmes External SharePoint.

7.67 Not all material referencing Confident Futures is subject to review. Marketing material viewed as a ‘template’ does not need to be reviewed each time it is subsequently used. Provider’s own working documents not intended as marketing material are also not subject to review. In these instances, it remains the responsibility of the provider to ensure the accuracy of material and correct referencing of Confident Futures. If, however, you are unsure if a specific item should be reviewed or not, contact your Performance Manager, who will be able to clarify this for you.

Social media

National media handling

Providers delivering more than one DWP provision

Use of DWP data

Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) system for Confident Futures

8.1 This chapter provides information on when and what actions are required in PRaP to record a start, exiting a Participant, PRaP 14 process and the removal of an incorrect or inappropriate referral for Confident Futures. This guidance should be read in conjunction with the User Productivity Kit and PRaP User Guide.

8.2 You must ensure that all information that is entered into PRaP is accurate, as in some instances, mistakes cannot be rectified by the PRaP Operational Digital and Database Support (PODDS) team.

8.3 Should there be any PRaP system issues you will be notified by the PODDS team directly and given clear instructions on what actions to take on PRaP.

8.4 Providers access PRaP via DWP Authenticate. Providers can download information to manage on their individual systems and update information about Participants progress into PRaP; payment claims, and calculations are generated automatically. Provider security requirements can be found on the contract Terms and Conditions page.

Receiving a PRaP referral

8.5 Following the Warm Handover, you will receive your PRaP referral from Jobcentre Plus within 2 working days. You must not work with any potential Participant without a PRaP referral.

8.6 If you have not received a PRaP referral you must contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC for either the Jobcentre Plus District or individual Jobcentre Plus site, depending upon the arrangements that you have in place. This will enable the PTWA to take corrective action and for the PRaP referral to be received before the Initial Meeting.

8.7 The referral will include an attached PDF document that will contain all the information that is relevant to the referral. This will include the Jobcentre ID, the Provider ID, the name and email address of the PTWA making the referral, and the Provision ID. Check that these are correct before you acknowledge the referral. Further information about the Participant information that you must check is detailed in this section acknowledging the referral.

Acknowledgment of the referral

8.8 Prior to acknowledging a referral, you must confirm that it is a Confident Futures opportunity. If the referral is anything other than a Confident Futures opportunity for example Restart, you must reject the referral and ask Jobcentre Plus to send a correct referral. Ensure that you use the appropriate rejection reasons.

8.9 You must check the PRaP referral, (include an attached PDF document) that will contain all the information that is relevant to the referral, ensuring that the data fields for the following are complete and correct:

name

address

contact telephone number

email address

National Insurance number

information relating to a need for additional support is recorded

the Potential Participant lives in England or Wales

the Jobcentre ID, the provider ID, the name and email address of the PTWA making the referral, and the Provision ID. Check that these are correct before you acknowledge the referral

This list is not exhaustive.

8.10 For further information see Chapter 2: Joining Confident Futures.

8.11 Should any information be missing from the referral contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC (PTWA) to request the outstanding information.

8.12 The following table describes further scenarios where you may identify that you cannot accept the referral prior to its acknowledgment:

Scenario Rejection Reason to be used on PRaP

The referral is a duplicate for example the Potential Participant is already engaged on Confident Futures. – The Potential Participant has engaged on Confident Futures Previously. Customer already on Provision (2)

The Potential Participant is employed/self-employed Excluded (5)

The Potential Participant is on another National DWP provision Customer not Eligible (3)

You have been previously contacted by the PTWA who has informed you that they have submitted a Confident Futures referral in Error Provision Unavailable (1)

Scenario not listed above Other (4)

8.13 Once the initial system checks have been completed you can acknowledge the referral in PRaP if appropriate.

8.14 You must allow at least one business day following acknowledgement of a referral before recording a start or a cancellation.

Rejecting a referral

You can cancel the referral, after acknowledging it, if any of the circumstances described in the table below, are applicable. Ensure that you use the appropriate rejection reasons.

Scenario Cancellation reason to be used on PRaP

You have made every attempt to engage with your Claimant, and they have not attended an initial face to face meeting after 15 working days from the date of the PRaP referral. If no contact has been made by day 40 the referral will automatically close in PRaP. Did not Attend (2)

For all other reasons including: – Duplicate referral – Participant has Previously engaged on Confident Futures – Participant is employed/self-employed – Referral made in error – The Participant is on another National DWP provision - Ineligible. Did not Start (4)

Note: A rejection or cancellation reason in PRaP cannot be rectified if mistakes are made. You must contact the Jobcentre SPoC and request a new referral.

8.15 For further information on this see Chapter 2: Joining Confident Futures.

8.16 A referral may be regarded as inappropriate where an error is identified after the referral has been made on PRaP by the PTWA, but prior to the date of the initial meeting. In such cases you should cancel the referral in PRaP and record the cancellation reason as “Did Not Start”. The provider should send a UCCF02 notification form to the Jobcentre Plus designated inbox to notify of the reason for cancellation.

Recording a Start in Confident Futures

8.17 You should hold an Initial Meeting with the Claimant within 15 working days of the date of referral using the Claimant’s preferred channel of engagement.

8.18 Where the initial meeting does not take place within 15 working days and you have not entered a Did Not Attend (DNA) code in PRaP, you may fail to meet CSS 1. If the Claimant is still interested you may still engage with the Participant, however, note that you only have 40 calendar days from the referral being made in which to register a start. Following this time, the line will automatically close in PRaP.

8.19 Following the completion of this Initial Meeting you must record a start.

8.20 You must record the start date as the date that the Initial Meeting took place and was completed.

8.21 Once the start date has been recorded in PRaP, the Participant will be working with you for the duration of their time on provision.

8.22 If the Claimant fails to attend their Initial Meeting and has not contacted, you in advance to explain why they will not be attending you should continue to make attempts to engage with the Claimant using the communication method agreed at the Warm Handover to achieve a start within 15 working days of referral.

8.23 If, after these repeated attempts to engage they have not participated in an Initial Meeting you should use the “Did Not Attend” cancellation reason in PRaP.

8.24 Where a DNA is recorded, the PTWA will follow up with the Claimant regarding the missed appointment and discuss whether a referral to the Provision remains appropriate. If it is considered appropriate a re-referral (following a DNA) can be made.

8.25 A re-referral shall not be considered in any circumstance after a Participant has been started on the Provision.

8.26 If the Claimant has attended their Initial meeting but does not, then start Provision you must enter a DNS in PRaP. For other reasons for recording a DNS refer to the relevant scenario table.

8.27 For further information see Chapter 2: Joining Confident Futures.

Auto closure of a PRaP referral

8.28 If after 40 calendar days you have taken no action to record a start, DNA or DNS as described above, the PRaP referral will automatically close.

8.29 Once the Participant has reached 365 days on Confident Futures their time on provision will automatically close in PRaP.

Note: Once a PRaP referral has automatically closed it cannot be reopened.

Early Completers due to a Change in Circumstances (CoC) UCCF01

8.30 If you receive a UCCF01 CoC form you must check the form for completeness. Should any information be missing, contact your PTWA or Jobcentre Plus SPoC for clarification.

8.31 Once a Participant is on Confident Futures, they can only be removed for the following reasons:

moves outside of England or Wales for a period longer than 90 calendar days, or a period that is expected to be longer than the Participant’s remaining time on Confident Futures

receives a custodial sentence and is residing at His Majesty’s Prison for a period longer than 90 calendar days

no longer has the right to work or reside in the UK

dies

moves into full-time education or training

moves into alternative DWP-funded provision

8.32 If none of the above reasons are given on the UCCF01 CoC form for removal from Confident Futures you must reject the form, take no further action in PRaP and contact the PTWA. You must continue to engage and support your Participant.

8.33 Participant may also choose to leave the programme for the following reasons:

support plan objectives achieved

moved into employment

deterioration in health condition

no longer wish to continue

8.34 If one of the reasons above are stated in the UCCF01 CoC form you can claim an end line in PRaP. You must use one of the following exit reasons:

Exit reason End code

Ineligible Must End because moves outside of England or Wales for a period longer than 90 calendar days, or a period that is expected to be longer than the Participant’s remaining time on Confident Futures 59

Ineligible Must End because receives a custodial sentence and is residing at His Majesty’s Prison for a period longer than 90 calendar days 59

Ineligible Must End because no longer has the right to work or reside in the UK 59

Ineligible Must End because dies 59

Moved into full time education/training - Must End 60

Moved to alternative DWP-funded provision - Must End 61

Disengaged - Must End 62

Support plan objectives achieved - End 63

Moved into employment - End 64

Deterioration in health condition - End 65

No longer wish to continue - End 66

8.35 You must ensure that you retain a copy of the UCCF01 CoC form for audit purposes. You must not exit a Participant on PRaP for any reasons other than those listed above.

8.36 If you exit a Participant by mistake in PRaP you should notify your Performance Manager to agree any possible next steps. You must continue to support your Participant during this time.

8.37 If the PTWA indicates one of the following reasons on a CoC UCCF01 form:

the Participant was in, and remains in, paid employment before the start was recorded

the Participant was identified as gainfully self-employed before the start was recorded

8.38 You must claim an end line (Line 5) using leaver reason Ineligible.

8.39 If a duplicate referral is identified, you must contact PODDS with the Participant’s PO number. You must not take any action in PRaP. PODDS will investigate and you will be advised as to the PO number requiring removal of the start line. Once this action has been completed by PODDS, you must cancel the referral using the ‘Did Not Start’ option in PRaP.

Six-Month Touchpoint and/or the End of Allotted Time

8.40 A Six-Month Touchpoint meeting will be held to review the Participant’s progress and for the Participant to decide whether to continue on the Provision. The final decision shall rest with the Participant. If the Participant is on a break at the Six-Month point, you should notify the PTWA of this, and the Six-Month Touchpoint should be arranged for a date within 20 working days of the end date of the break.

8.41 If the Participant decides to complete their time on Confident Futures at this point you should ship the end line using the appropriate end code outlined above.

MI capture

8.42 The appropriate end line should then be shipped in PRaP (as detailed above).

Management Information (MI) lines

8.43 Three MI lines to support CSS 2 and CSS 3 have been introduced to collect data for confident futures, which will require the provider to “ship” the MI line once the provider feels they have achieved each CSS, those CSS’s are:

CSS 2 - The date of the Completion of Initial Support Plan

CSS 3 - The date of the Completion of the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting

CSS 3 - The date of completion of the Support Plan being shared with the Participant following the Six-Month Touchpoint

Note: In exceptional circumstances, and at the request of the Participant the completion of the Six-Months Touchpoint may occur before day 182 in this situation CSS 3 MI line will only be able to be claimed after day 182.

8.44 Claiming the MI lines for CSS 2 and or CSS 3 will generate an outcome payment of £0.01 each.

PRaP 14 Process for the Confident Futures or identification of inappropriate referrals following a start

8.45 Following your Participant’s start on Confident Futures, the PTWA or DWP Live Running Policy team may identify an inappropriate or duplicate referral.

8.46 The PRaP 14 process is used to remove the inappropriate or duplicate referral from PRAP in the limited circumstances, as described below.

8.47 The PRAP 14 process cannot be used for the incorrect recording of start dates, outcomes recording end dates or ending participation in error. In these scenarios, mistakes cannot be rectified.

8.48 It is important that the appropriate action is taken where the PTWA indicates one of the following reasons on a Change of Circumstances Notification form UCCF01:

the Participant was in, and remains in, paid employment before the start was recorded

the Participant was identified as gainfully self-employed before the start was recorded

the Participant has been referred to the wrong provision, and a new referral is required by the Jobcentre Plus Work Coach to the correct provision

8.49 You may be contacted by the DWP Live Running Policy team where they have identified that:

(a) The Participant has already participated in the Confident Futures.

(b) The Participant is engaged on another provision, for example Restart and/or Connect to Work.

8.50 Upon notification from the PTWA or DWP Live Running Policy team, you must:

(a) Claim an end line (Line 5) in PRaP using the appropriate leaver code.

(b) Complete a PRAP 14 using the appropriate dropdown reason and email it to PODDS prap.support@dwp.gov.uk.

8.51 Once the action has been completed by PODDS, you must cancel the referral and claim ‘Did Not Start’.

8.52 If you identify a duplicate referral, a referral made on the wrong opportunity, or that the Participant is engaged on another provision, you must:

(a) Claim the end line (Line 5) using the appropriate leaver code.

(b) Complete the PRAP 14 and using the appropriate dropdown reason and email it to PODDS prap.support@dwp.gov.uk.

(c) Once the action has been completed by PODDS, you must cancel the referral and claim ‘Did Not Start’.

(d) Where the Participant has been referred to the wrong opportunity, you must contact the Jobcentre Plus SPoC and request that a new referral is made to the correct opportunity.

(e) Where the Participant has previously participated or is engaged on another provision, ensure that the Participant’s PTWA is informed via a UCCF02 notification form and signpost the Participant back to Jobcentre Plus.

(f) Where you identify a duplicate referral, you must ensure that action is only taken on the referral that was created after the original referral was received.

Chapter 9: Confident Futures contract metrics, managing performance and risk assurance

9.1 This chapter covers your contract metrics how we will manage performance of Confident Futures. To do this, we will apply our Performance Management Intervention Regime (PMIR) - a structured and escalating process, over 4 levels, of interaction and intervention, focusing on both a qualitative and quantitative assessment of your performance. We will also undertake reviews of your risk management controls, and your systems and processes through our Provider Assurance Team (PAT).

Performance and the performance metrics

9.2 From the start of your contract, you are expected to achieve each of the Performance Metrics. These are the:

Customer Service Standards

Outputs

Performance delivery and expectations

9.3 Throughout the life of the contract, we will review your performance and compliance in each of the above areas. To do this, we will use our available management information, whether from our systems and/or from the PCO checks, the Management Information that you provide, and the approach detailed in our PMIR.

9.4 If any of the above Metrics are not achieved, whether that’s on an in-month, rolling, cohort, or cumulative basis, we may consider using an appropriate contract lever as detailed within your contract or in respect of Outputs, withhold payment as described in chapter 4. We may also consider recovering any costs we incur because of our performance improvement activity with you, again as detailed in your contract.

Outputs

9.5 There are 3 Outputs as set out in annex 8 of the Confident Futures specification:

1. Monthly Performance Return – using the template provided by DWP, providers will submit this return by 5th working day of each month as detailed in Supplier Management Information paragraphs 4.33 to 4.39 of Confident Futures Specification.

2. Participant Support Summary – a quarterly submission providing an aggregated, descriptive overview support delivered across the quarter using Support Plans and Progress Reports. The summary will provide insight into the support services being provided to participants, use of partners and local services, participant engagement insights and your response to disengagement.

3. Delivery Review Plan and Reports – providers must submit the Delivery Review Plan within 40 working days of contract start and 6 monthly thereafter. These reports will outline how the provider will assess the effectiveness of their delivery; identify and prioritise areas for improvement; implement refinements; and monitor the impact of changes over time. The Delivery Review Report will outline how the provider has reviewed the effectiveness of their delivery; what improvements have been identified and implemented; how the provider has utilised learning including learning shared across the network of prime providers; and assessed the impact of changes made.

Customer Service Standards (CSSs)

9.6 There are 3 Customer Service Standards (CSSs), that we expect you to deliver against, within this contract.

Description of Customer Service Standard System used for measurement and % of achievement to meet Customer Service Standard

Customer Service Standard 1 (CSS 1) - The Supplier shall ensure that a CF Initial Meeting is conducted with a Participant via their preferred channel of engagement; in-person, video, or phone and a CF Start/Did Not Start/Did Not Attend is recorded on Information Communication Technology (ICT) systems. DWP Information Technology (IT) systems and PCO checks will provide assurance. 95% of cases within 15 working days of the referral (date of referral is counted as day zero). The Supplier shall meet 100% of target.

Customer Service Standard 2 (CSS 2) - The Supplier shall start an Initial Support Plan with the Participant at the Initial Meeting and finalise this Initial Support Plan within 15 working days of that meeting, informed by a Needs Assessment and information shared at the Warm Handover meeting. DWP IT systems and PCO checks will provide assurance. For 97% of Participants who start the programme.

Customer Service Standard 3 (CSS 3) - The Supplier shall ensure that the DA leads a Six-Month Touchpoint meeting in respect of each Participant except those Participants who are no longer UC Claimants. The Six-Month Touchpoint meeting shall be attended by the DA, the Participant and the Pathways to Work Adviser. The Supplier shall ensure that, within 10 working days of the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting being completed: (1) the Support Plan is updated; and (2) the outcome and agreed next steps from the Six-Month Touchpoint meeting are captured and shared with the Participant. DWP IT systems and PCO checks will provide assurance. For 100% of active Participants

9.7 We will use a mixture of Management Information (MI) held on DWP systems, findings from our PCO checks, and provider reported management information, to review your performance against the CSSs.

9.8 Performance against each CSS will be monitored and form a key part of your Contract Performance Review (CPR) discussion with your Performance Manager including if performance improvement activity is required and why.

Customer Satisfaction measure survey activity information

9.9 DWP will monitor the level of customer satisfaction with the Confident Futures programme through a survey undertaken independently of providers at the 6 and 12-month points of Provision duration.

9.10 Providers are also expected to carry out Participant Insight each month to obtain information on the usefulness of the programme by asking all Participants how satisfied they are with Confident Futures. The full question and set responses are included in schedule 4a, paragraph 1, of the contract. Providers are to report the participant insight to the Authority by the 15th day of the calendar month.

9.11 Both the provider reported insight, and the independent participant survey will be discussed during CPRs.

Performance Management Intervention Regime (PMIR)

9.12 The DWP operates a robust PMIR, the aim is to provide support and hold you accountable for achievement of the performance metrics stipulated in your contract.

9.13 You are expected to meet as a minimum, the performance levels as stipulated in your contract, and we will consider formal action where such performance levels are not met.

9.14 You will need to provide us with a named contact who will work with our DWP Performance Manager to ensure the performance metrics at CPA level are achieved.

9.15 There are 4 levels of the PMIR which can run independently or concurrently, and we will take action at any level, at any time. For example, we will be entitled to take formal action at Level 4 whether or not the steps outlined at levels 1, 2 and/or 3 were taken.

9.16 The PMIR framework will be used to address under performance, however, nothing in the PMIR will prejudice the remedies available to DWP for failure to meet any Performance Metrics.

Level 1: Standard Performance Intervention Stage

Level 2: Enhanced Performance Intervention Stage

Level 3: Heightened Performance Intervention Stage

Level 4: Critical Performance Intervention Stage

9.17 Your CPA must have in place an EAD Action Plan submitted by your Contract Operational Lead to the Performance Manager regardless of what intervention level you are in. The EAD Action Plan is required to be in place immediately following the contract implementation period (from contract go live).

9.18 The purpose of the provider Action Plan is to provide us with assurance that you have identified the top priority areas for improvement. All actions in the plan should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound (SMART) and any longer-term actions should incorporate SMART milestone targets. Your Performance Manager will work with you to ensure your Action Plan aligns with information submitted to the department in support of Outputs 1 to 3 of your contract.

9.19 Your Performance Manager will work closely with you throughout each level of intervention. The frequency of meetings, scope and types of activity listed within Intervention Level 1 below increasing where improvements are not seen.

9.20 Your Performance Manager will hold regular CPRs with you at CPA level, focussing on the performance against quantitative and qualitative aspects of the contract including, but not limited to, in-month, rolling 3-months, rolling 12-month cohort or cumulative basis from day 1 of the contract. More detail on CPRs is covered in Annex 9.1.

Performance Compliance Officers (PCOs) and their checks

The Provider Assurance Team (PAT)

Background and purpose

9.45 The primary purpose of the DWP Contract Management and Partner Delivery (CMPD) Provider Assurance Team (PAT) is to provide the DWP with assurance that providers’ systems of internal control are such that payments made to CMPD providers are in accordance with DWP’s and the Treasury’s requirements.

9.46 PAT reviews test Providers’ internal control systems to establish how effective they are at managing risk to DWP in relation to CMPD expenditure and service delivery including, the arrangements they have with supply chain partners.

9.47 PAT will review providers’ internal control systems to assess their ability to manage risk across the following key areas:

Governance Arrangements - this covers the providers’ governance arrangements, their systems for tracking and reporting performance and their anti-fraud measures, along with the management of any supply chain partners

Service Delivery - this includes the providers’ systems for starting, ending and moving Participants through provision and aims to ensure that DWP receives the service it pays for

Claim Procedures and Payments - this aims to ensure that providers have effective systems in place to support claims for payment, including segregation of duties where appropriate

How PAT operates

9.48 The PAT operates at a national level enabling it to present CMPD provision providers operating across regions with a single view of the effectiveness of their systems. Each provider is allocated a nominated Senior Assurance Manager as a SPoC within DWP for management of assurance related issues or concerns. Refer to Contact details for the team for information.

9.49 On completion of each review providers are awarded a PAT assurance rating in one of the following 4 categories:

(a) weak

(b) limited

(c) reasonable

(d) strong

9.50 The provider is sent a formal report which details the review findings including key strengths and areas for improvement, and where weaknesses have been identified. providers are required to complete an action plan setting out appropriate steps for improvement. Action plans are followed up until the PAT is satisfied that all required actions have been undertaken.

9.51 The description of the 4 assurance levels are as follows:

Strong Assurance – governance, risk management and control arrangements operated provide strong assurance that material risks are identified and managed efficiently and effectively, although improvements may be recommended

Reasonable Assurance – governance, risk management and control arrangements operated provide reasonable assurance that material risks are identified and managed efficiently and effectively. Remedial action is required to improve the control environment

Limited Assurance – governance, risk management and control arrangements operated provide limited assurance that material risks are identified and managed efficiently and effectively. Corrective action is required to resolve control weaknesses

Weak Assurance – governance, risk management and control arrangements operated provide weak assurance that material risks are identified and managed effectively. Urgent and significant corrective action is required to resolve significant control weaknesses

PAT planning

9.52 In order to manage review activity and direct resources in the most effective way, the PAT operates a national plan covering all health and employment provision providers in scope for PAT reviews. Provider reviews are allocated in priority order according to risk. This is determined by a number of factors including the current assurance rating, length of time since the previous review, and DWP stakeholder intelligence.

The review process

9.53 There are 5 stages to the review process which can take up to 23 weeks to complete, depending on the complexity of the providers organisation and the extent of the health or employment provision contracts. The bulk of provider facing activity takes place within field testing which generally lasts no longer than 5 weeks.

Provider review process

9.54 A PAT review covers the following stages:

planning and research

initial evaluation

field work

final evaluation

reporting

follow up of action plan

Planning research and Initial Evaluation

9.55 The purpose of this stage is to pull together all relevant information about the PAT review, to form a paper-based opinion about the systems and develop the testing strategy.

9.56 During this period, you will be sent 2 documents:

a Provider Systems Questionnaire (PSQ) which asks a series of questions about your systems across each of the 3 scope areas

a site information stencil to confirm information about the delivery sites for the programmes.

9.57 The PAT also take account of feedback from other departmental colleagues who work closely with you. Intelligence is gathered from these sources during the planning process and used alongside the PSQ response from you when forming an initial view of the risk and development of the test strategy.

Field work

9.58 Commencement of the field work is signalled by a formal start-up meeting between the provider and the PAT. The purpose of this meeting is to brief you on the forthcoming review and agree the terms of engagement throughout including timescales for final feedback and the timeframe for providing all evidence by.

9.59 Based on the planning, research and initial evaluation, the PAT decide whether to carry out any testing deemed necessary to form a judgement as to the effectiveness of the systems under review.

9.60 Field Testing is arranged via Microsoft Teams and at your premises or a combination of both. Where fieldwork is to be undertaken at your premises, it can be conducted at any of the sites across the country. Choosing which premises to visit will be determined by a number of factors, for example the provisions and activities delivered at individual sites, any intelligence gathered during the planning stage which may indicate weaknesses in certain areas, or the availability of the PAT resource.

9.61 The tests will typically include reviewing key policy documents, examining participant files, interviewing staff, and performing checks in sufficient quantities to allow the team to form an opinion across your systems as a whole. This may mean that testing has to be extended in some circumstances or that it may be cut short in others.

9.62 During the testing period the PAT provides a written summary of the key points. This allows you to understand and discuss the findings to date.

9.63 Throughout the testing period you will be given the opportunity to provide any supporting documentation and/or missing evidence that has been requested by the PAT. All evidence must be provided by the date agreed at the start up meeting.

Final evaluation

9.64 Evaluation of your systems is continuous throughout the end-to-end PAT review process. Once testing is complete all the findings are considered, and an overall assurance level is awarded covering the 3 scope areas of Governance Arrangements, Service Delivery and Claims Procedures and Payments.

9.65 The final evaluation and assurance level will be formally presented to you at a final feedback meeting at a time agreed in advance. At this meeting the PAT will discuss what actions will need to be taken to address any issues raised and timescales for satisfactory completion of those actions.

Review outputs

9.66 Following the final feedback, a report is produced by the PAT and sent to you. The report will contain details of findings and opinion against all key risk areas across the 3 scope areas and an overall assurance level assessment for the PAT report.

9.67 There will be an action plan at the back of the report covering all the issues raised at the feedback meeting. You are expected to return the action plan within 10 working days of receipt. The response should contain any timescales for implementing any necessary improvements, which can be from one week to a maximum of 3 months.

9.68 The PAT will work with you to implement all the actions. It is the PAT that make the final decision on and sign off each action. This follow up will take place within the timescales agreed with the PAT.

9.69 You are also asked to complete and return a feedback stencil to the Senior Assurance Manager (SAM). DWP is committed to providing an effective Provider Assurance function and in order to meet this commitment the PAT need to constantly review the way in which they operate and their supporting policies and procedures. As a major stakeholder in this process, obtaining feedback from you is critical.

9.70 If there are any issues or causes for concern that cannot be addressed throughout the course of the review, then the provider should in the first instance put a complaint in writing to the Head of the PAT. There is no formal appeals process to allow you to challenge the level of assurance awarded. The PAT undertake a period of extensive evaluation to ensure there is a good understanding of your systems and processes and will gain sufficient evidence through testing to reach a sound conclusion regarding the adequacy and effectiveness of the controls within your organisation. If you are unhappy with the outcome there will be the opportunity to discuss concerns with the SAM and/or Head of the PAT.

9.71 The final feedback meeting allows you ample opportunity to discuss the findings and assurance level, before the final report is issued.

9.72 The main focus of any meeting or correspondence after an assurance rating has been given will concentrate on the implementation of the areas for improvement as detailed in the action plan to strengthen your controls/ maintain a strong level of control in preparation for your next review.

9.73 The report is also sent to DWP stakeholders, these typically include (but not exclusively):

CMPD Director

Commercial Directorate

Employment Accounts Division or Team Personal Independent Payment (PIP)

Counter Fraud and Investigation

PRaP Operational Digital and Database Support (PODDS) team

Other potential actions

9.74 Without prejudice to any other of DWP’s rights under your Contracts, there may be other actions required depending on the findings of the review, including:

Overpayment Recovery – if overpayments are identified and evidence could not be produced during the review, then DWP may seek to recover any overpayments; and

if any overpayments, errors or discrepancies identified during the review indicate they are as a result of systemic weaknesses then you may be required to provide the applicable evidence over a specified period of time and in doing so identify any overpayments. The results will be verified before any subsequent action is taken

9.75 For payments where an error rate has already been extrapolated backtracking and recovery action will not be applicable.

PAT reporting

9.76 DWP may periodically publish assurance levels by provider (note - this will not include reports or supporting information).

9.77 All PAT reports are shared with the CMPD Director and other senior managers within DWP.

9.78 DWP may take remedial actions in the following circumstances:

if following a Weak or Limited Assurance level from the PAT your subsequent assurance level is the same or worse for the same reasons, or you are awarded a consecutive third week or limited assurance, regardless of the reasons

following a review, if you fail to submit and/or implement the Action Plan within agreed timescale

where there are suspicions that you may be acting inappropriately the team will refer to Counter Fraud and Investigations as the experts trained in the legalities and techniques required to carry out formal investigations

where there are serious concerns around data security these are reported through the respective channels to colleagues in the DWP Security Incident Response Team
